title.raw: 卷四十九 列傳第三十七: 朱瑞 叱列延慶 斛斯椿 賈顯度 樊子鵠 侯深 賀拔允 侯莫陳悅 念賢 梁覽 雷紹 毛遐 乙弗朗 Volume 49 Biographies 37: Zhu rui, Chilie Yanqing, Hu Sichun, Jia Xiandu, Fan Zihu, Hou Shen, He Bayun, Houmo Chenyue, Nian Xian, Liang Lan, Lei Shao, Mao Xia, Yi Fulang

translations.literal: Zhu Rui, Chilie Yanqing, Hu Sichun, Jia Xiandu, Fan Zihu, Hou Shen, He Bayun, Houmo Chenyue, Nian Xian, Liang Lan, Lei Shao, Mao Xia, and Yi Fulang
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rui; Chilie Yanqing; Hu Sichun; Jia Xiandu; Fan Zihu; Hou Shen; He Bayun; Houmo Chenyue; Nian Xian; Liang Lan; Lei Shao; Mao Xia; and Yi Fulang

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十七

translations.literal: Biographies, number thirty-seven
translations.idiomatic: Biography 37

sentences.zh: 朱瑞叱列延慶斛斯椿子徵孫政賈顯度弟智樊子鵠侯深賀拔允弟勝勝弟岳侯莫陳悅念賢梁覽雷紹毛遐弟鴻賓乙弗朗

translations.literal: Zhu Rui; Chilie Yanqing; Hu Sichun, his son Zheng, his grandson Zheng; Jia Xiandu, his younger brother Zhi; Fan Zihu; Hou Shen; He Bayun, his younger brother Sheng, Sheng's younger brother Yue; Houmo Chenyue; Nian Xian; Liang Lan; Lei Shao; Mao Xia, his younger brother Hongbin; Yi Fulang
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rui; Chilie Yanqing; Hu Sichun, with his son Zheng and grandson Zheng; Jia Xiandu and his younger brother Zhi; Fan Zihu; Hou Shen; He Bayun, his younger brother Sheng, and Sheng's younger brother Yue; Houmo Chenyue; Nian Xian; Liang Lan; Lei Shao; Mao Xia and his younger brother Hongbin; and Yi Fulang

sentences.zh: 朱瑞，字元龍，代郡桑乾人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Rui, styled Yuanlong, was a native of Sanggan in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rui, courtesy name Yuanlong, came from Sanggan in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖就，沛縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiu was magistrate of Pei County.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiu had served as magistrate of Pei County.

sentences.zh: 父惠，行太原太守。

translations.literal: His father Hui acted as Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui had held the acting post of Administrator of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 瑞貴達，並贈刺史。

translations.literal: When Rui rose to eminence, both were posthumously enfeoffed as regional inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: After Rui rose to high rank, both forebears were posthumously granted the title of regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 瑞長厚質直，敬愛人士，爾硃榮引為大行台郎中，甚見親任，以為黃門侍郎，仍中書舍人。

translations.literal: Rui was generous, sincere, and upright by nature and respected men of talent. Erzhu Rong brought him in as a director of the Grand March Secretariat and greatly favored and trusted him, appointing him Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and also Attendant Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Rui was generous, forthright, and upright, and he held scholars in esteem. Erzhu Rong recruited him as a director of the Grand March Secretariat, came to rely on him deeply, and made him Gentleman at the Yellow Gates while also keeping him on as Attendant Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 榮恐朝廷事意有所不知，故居之門下，為腹心之寄。

translations.literal: Rong feared that matters and intentions at court might escape his knowledge, and therefore kept Rui at his side as a man in whom he could confide his innermost thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Rong worried that he might not learn of affairs and intentions at court, so he kept Rui at his side as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 封陽邑縣公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He received the title Duke of Yangyi County.

sentences.zh: 及元顥內逼，從車駕于河陽，除侍中、兼吏部尚書，改封北海郡公。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Rui followed the imperial carriage to Heyang and was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrent Minister of Personnel, his fief being changed to Duke of Beihai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao advanced on the capital, Rui accompanied the imperial carriage to Heyang and was made Palace Attendant and concurrent Minister of Personnel, with his title changed to Duke of Beihai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還洛，改封樂陵郡公，仍侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to Luoyang, Rui's fief was changed to Duke of Leling Commandery, and he remained Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang returned to Luoyang, Rui was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Leling Commandery and kept his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 瑞雖為爾硃榮所委，而善處朝廷間。

translations.literal: Although Rui had been entrusted by Erzhu Rong, he knew how to conduct himself well between court and the Erzhu faction.
translations.idiomatic: Though Rui had been a man of Erzhu Rong's trust, he handled relations between the court and the Erzhu clan with tact.

sentences.zh: 帝亦賞遇之，嘗謂侍臣曰：「為人臣當須忠實，至如硃元龍者，朕待之亦不異餘人。」

translations.literal: The emperor also favored him and once told his attendants, "As a subject one must be loyal and sincere. As for a man like Zhu Yuanlong, I treat him no differently from anyone else."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued him as well and once told his attendants, "A subject ought to be loyal and true-hearted. As for someone like Zhu Yuanlong, I do not treat him any differently from my other ministers."

sentences.zh: 瑞以青州樂陵有硃氏，意欲歸之，故求為青州中正。

translations.literal: Because there was a Zhu clan at Leling in Qing Province, Rui wished to be affiliated with it and therefore requested appointment as chief arbiter of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Rui knew that a Zhu lineage existed at Leling in Qing Province and wished to join it, so he asked to be made chief arbiter of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 又以滄州樂陵亦有硃氏，而心好河北，遂乞三從內並屬滄州樂陵郡。

translations.literal: Because Leling in Cang Province also had a Zhu clan and his heart favored Hebei, he then petitioned that all his relatives within three degrees of mourning be registered under Leling Commandery in Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Zhu clan at Leling in Cang Province, and as he preferred Hebei, he petitioned to have all his kin within three degrees of mourning registered under Leling in Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，仍轉滄州大中正。

translations.literal: An edict approved this, and he was transferred to be chief arbiter of Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted his request and transferred him to serve as chief arbiter of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，瑞與世隆俱北走。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Rui fled north together with Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Rui fled north with Shilong.

sentences.zh: 以莊帝待之素厚，且見世隆等並無雄才，終當敗喪，于路乃還，帝大悅。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Zhuang had always treated him generously, and because he saw that Shilong and the others lacked heroic talent and would in the end meet defeat and ruin, he turned back on the road. The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering how generously Emperor Zhuang had always treated him, and seeing that Shilong and his party lacked real ability and were bound for ruin, he turned back on the road. The emperor was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 時爾硃天光擁眾關右，帝招納之，乃以瑞兼尚書左僕射，為西道大行台，以慰勞焉。

translations.literal: At that time Erzhu Tianguang held a large force in the Guanzhong region, and the emperor sought to win him over. Rui was therefore made concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand March Commissioner of the Western Route to console and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Tianguang then commanded a large army in the west, and the emperor wished to win him over. Rui was appointed concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and sent west as Grand March Commissioner to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 既達長安，會爾硃兆入洛，復還京師。

translations.literal: After he reached Chang'an, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, and he returned once more to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had reached Chang'an when Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, so he returned to the capital again.

sentences.zh: 都督斛斯椿先與瑞有隙，數譖之於世隆，世隆遂誅之。

translations.literal: The commander Hu Sichun had long borne a grudge against Rui and repeatedly slandered him to Shilong, whereupon Shilong had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Hu Sichun had long been at odds with Rui and repeatedly slandered him to Shilong, who then had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈開府儀同三司、青州刺史，諡曰恭穆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taichang era he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and made Regional Inspector of Qing Province, with the posthumous name Gongmu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and as Regional Inspector of Qing Province, with the posthumous name Gongmu.

sentences.zh: 叱列延慶，代西部人也，世為酋帥。

translations.literal: Chilie Yanqing was a man of the western part of Dai and for generations had been a tribal chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Chilie Yanqing came from western Dai, where his family had been tribal chieftains for generations.

sentences.zh: 延慶娶爾硃世隆姊，故被爾硃榮親遇。

translations.literal: Yanqing married Erzhu Shilong's elder sister and therefore received Erzhu Rong's personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing had married Erzhu Shilong's elder sister, which won him Erzhu Rong's personal favor.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，世隆得志，特見委重，兼尚書左僕射、山東行台、北海郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Putai era, when Shilong had achieved his ambitions, Yanqing was especially entrusted with weighty duties as concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand March Commissioner of Shandong, and Duke of Beihai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era, once Shilong had gained power, Yanqing was especially trusted with concurrent posts as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand March Commissioner of Shandong, and Duke of Beihai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時幽州刺史劉靈助以莊帝幽崩，遂舉兵唱義，世隆白節閔帝，以延慶與大都督侯深于定州討之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Lingzhu, Regional Inspector of You Province, raised troops in the name of righteousness because Emperor Zhuang had died in You Province. Shilong reported this to Emperor Jiemin and sent Yanqing together with the Grand Commander Hou Shen to suppress him in Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingzhu, Regional Inspector of You Province, took up arms in the name of righteousness after Emperor Zhuang died in You. Shilong reported this to Emperor Jiemin and sent Yanqing with Grand Commander Hou Shen to attack him in Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 深以靈助善占，百姓信惑，未易可圖，欲還師入據關拒險，以待其變。

translations.literal: Hou Shen held that because Lingzhu was skilled at divination the common people believed and were bewildered by him, so he would not be easy to overcome. He wished to withdraw the army, enter and hold a pass, rely on difficult terrain, and wait for changes in the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shen argued that Lingzhu's skill at divination had won the people's trust and made him hard to defeat, and proposed withdrawing into a fortified pass and waiting for circumstances to change.

sentences.zh: 延慶以靈助庸人，彼皆恃其妖術，坐看符厭，寧肯戮力致死。

translations.literal: Yanqing said that Lingzhu was a mediocre man and that his followers all relied on his sorcery, merely watching for omens and talismans—how would they be willing to fight to the death with all their strength?
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing replied that Lingzhu was a mediocrity whose followers trusted only his sorcery and omens and would never fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 宜詭言西歸，可襲而禽。

translations.literal: They should falsely announce a withdrawal to the west; then he could be taken by surprise and captured.
translations.idiomatic: They should feign a withdrawal to the west and then take him by surprise.

sentences.zh: 深從之，乃出頓城西，聲雲將還，詰朝造靈助壘，遂破禽之。

translations.literal: Hou Shen agreed. They then marched out and encamped west of the city, proclaiming that they would withdraw. At dawn the next day they attacked Lingzhu's camp, broke his force, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shen agreed. They marched out and camped west of the city, announcing a withdrawal; at dawn the next day they stormed Lingzhu's camp, routed him, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵戰敗，延慶與爾硃仲遠走度石濟。

translations.literal: When they were defeated at Hanling, Yanqing fled with Erzhu Zhongyuan and crossed the Stone Ford.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Hanling, Yanqing fled with Erzhu Zhongyuan and crossed the Stone Ford.

sentences.zh: 仲遠南竄，延慶北降齊神武，仍從并州。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan fled south, while Yanqing surrendered in the north to Duke Shenwu of Qi and thereafter followed him to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan fled south; Yanqing surrendered to Gao Huan in the north and followed him to Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 後赴洛，孝武帝以為中軍大都督。

translations.literal: Later he went to Luoyang, and Emperor Xiaowu appointed him Grand Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He later went to Luoyang, where Emperor Xiaowu made him Grand Commander of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 孝武之西，齊神武誅之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Duke Shenwu of Qi had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Gao Huan had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿，字法壽，廣牧富昌人也。

translations.literal: Hu Sichun, styled Fashou, was a native of Fuchang in Guangmu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sichun, courtesy name Fashou, came from Fuchang in Guangmu.

sentences.zh: 其先世為莫弗大人。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations had been tribal chiefs bearing the title Mofu daren.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had for generations held the tribal title Mofu daren.

sentences.zh: 父足，一名敦，明帝時為左牧令。

translations.literal: His father Zu, also called Dun, served in Emperor Ming's time as Director of the Left Pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zu, also known as Dun, had been Director of the Left Pasturage under Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 時河西賊起，牧人不安，椿乃將家投爾硃榮。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in the Hexi region and the pastoral peoples were unsettled. Chun therefore took his family and submitted to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in the Hexi region and the pastoral peoples were thrown into turmoil, Chun took his family and joined Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 征伐有功，稍遷中散大夫，署外兵事。

translations.literal: He achieved merit in campaigns and was gradually promoted to Palace Attendant and assigned to military affairs outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He won distinction in campaigns and was gradually promoted to Palace Attendant with responsibility for forces outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 椿性佞巧，甚得榮心，軍之密謀，頗亦關預。

translations.literal: Chun was sycophantic and crafty by nature and won Rong's heart; he also took part in many of the army's secret plans.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty and ingratiating by nature, Chun won Rong's trust and was drawn into many of the army's secret counsels.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，改封陽曲縣公，除榮大將軍府司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign his fief was changed to Duke of Yangqu County and he was appointed Chief of Staff in Rong's Grand General's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yangqu County and made Chief of Staff in Rong's Grand General's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後為東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He later became Regional Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Regional Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及榮死，椿甚憂懼。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Chun was deeply anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death, Chun was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 時梁以汝南王悅為魏主，資其士馬，次於境上。

translations.literal: At that time Liang supported the Prince of Runan, Yuan Yue, as ruler of Wei and supplied him with troops and horses, stationing them on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was then backing Yuan Yue, Prince of Runan, as ruler of Wei and had supplied him with troops and horses massed on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 椿遂棄州歸悅。

translations.literal: Chun therefore abandoned his province and went over to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Chun abandoned his province and went over to Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅授尚書左僕射、司空公，封靈丘郡公，又為大行台前驅都督。

translations.literal: Yue appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Works, enfeoffed him as Duke of Lingqiu Commandery, and also made him vanguard commander of the Grand March Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yue made him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Works, enfeoffed him as Duke of Lingqiu Commandery, and appointed him vanguard commander of the Grand March Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會爾硃兆入洛，悅知不逮，南旋。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Yue knew he could not prevail and withdrew south.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Yue saw he could not prevail and withdrew south.

sentences.zh: 椿復背悅歸兆。

translations.literal: Chun again turned against Yue and returned to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Chun deserted Yue once more and went over to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以參立節閔謀，拜侍中、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，封城陽郡公。

translations.literal: For taking part in the plan to enthrone Emperor Jiemin, he was appointed Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed as Duke of Chengyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For helping to enthrone Emperor Jiemin, he was made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed as Duke of Chengyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was further granted the title of Grand Master with Golden Tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further granted the title of Grand Master with Golden Tally.

sentences.zh: 時椿父足先在秀容，忽有傳其死問，椿請減己階以贈之。

translations.literal: At that time Chun's father Zu was still at Xiurong when word suddenly came that he had died. Chun asked to reduce his own rank in order to confer posthumous honors on him.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's father Zu was still at Xiurong when a report suddenly arrived that he had died. Chun asked to reduce his own rank so that honors could be conferred on his father.

sentences.zh: 尋知其父猶存，詔復官，仍除其父為車騎將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon it was learned that his father was still alive. An edict restored Chun's rank, and his father was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: It soon turned out that his father was still alive. An edict restored Chun's rank and appointed his father General of Chariots and Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 椿以爾硃兆擅權，懼禍，乃與賀拔勝俱說世隆以正道。

translations.literal: Because Erzhu Zhao monopolized power, Chun feared disaster and, together with Heba Sheng, urged Shilong to follow the right path.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disaster from Erzhu Zhao's monopoly of power, Chun joined Heba Sheng in urging Shilong to take the righteous course.

sentences.zh: 世隆不悅，欲害椿，賴爾硃天光救，得免。

translations.literal: Shilong was displeased and wished to kill Chun, but thanks to Erzhu Tianguang's rescue he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong took offense and wanted to kill Chun, but Erzhu Tianguang saved him.

sentences.zh: 及世隆、度律與兆自相疑，椿與賀拔勝和之，兆執椿、勝還營。

translations.literal: When Shilong and Dulü became mutually suspicious of Zhao, Chun and Heba Sheng mediated between them. Zhao seized Chun and Sheng and took them back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilong and Dulü grew suspicious of Zhao, Chun and Heba Sheng tried to mediate. Zhao seized them both and took them back to camp.

sentences.zh: 椿又陳以正理，兆謝而遣之。

translations.literal: Chun again set forth the right principles, and Zhao apologized and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Chun again argued on principle, and Zhao apologized and let them go.

sentences.zh: 椿謂勝曰：「天下皆怨毒爾硃，吾等附之，亡無日矣，不如圖之。」

translations.literal: Chun said to Sheng, "All under Heaven resent and hate the Erzhu. If we cling to them, our destruction will come any day now. We had better plot against them."
translations.idiomatic: Chun told Sheng, "All the realm hates the Erzhu clan. If we stay attached to them, we are doomed. We should plot against them."

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「天光與兆，各據一方，今俱禽為難。」

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Tianguang and Zhao each hold a region. To seize both at once would be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "Tianguang and Zhao each hold a separate region. Taking both at once would be hard."

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「易致耳。」

translations.literal: Chun said, "That is easy to bring about."
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "That is easy enough."

sentences.zh: 乃說世隆追天光等赴洛，討齊神武。

translations.literal: He then persuaded Shilong to summon Tianguang and the others to Luoyang to campaign against Duke Shenwu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He then persuaded Shilong to summon Tianguang and the others to Luoyang to attack Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵之敗，椿謂都督賈顯智等曰：「若不先執爾硃，我等死無類矣。」

translations.literal: After the defeat at Hanling, Chun said to the commander Jia Xianzhi and the others, "If we do not seize the Erzhu first, we shall die without remnant."
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Hanling, Chun told Commander Jia Xianzhi and the others, "Unless we seize the Erzhu first, none of us will survive."

sentences.zh: 遂與顯智等夜于桑下盟約，倍道兼行。

translations.literal: He then made a pact with Xianzhi and the others at night beneath mulberry trees and pressed forward at double speed.
translations.idiomatic: That night he swore an oath with Xianzhi and the others under mulberry trees and marched at forced speed.

sentences.zh: 椿入北中城，收爾硃部曲，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Chun entered Beizhong Fortress, gathered the Erzhu troops, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Chun entered Beizhong Fortress, rounded up the Erzhu troops, and slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 令弟元壽與張歡、長孫承業、顯智等襲世隆、彥伯兄弟，並斬於閶闔門外。

translations.literal: He ordered his younger brother Yuanshou, together with Zhang Huan, Zhangsun Chengye, Xianzhi, and the others, to strike at Shilong and the Yanbo brothers, and all were beheaded outside the Chang-le Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his younger brother Yuanshou with Zhang Huan, Zhangsun Chengye, Xianzhi, and the others to attack Shilong and the Yanbo brothers, and all were beheaded outside the Chang-le Gate.

sentences.zh: 椿入洛，縣世隆兄弟首于其門樹。

translations.literal: When Chun entered Luoyang, he hung the heads of Shilong and his brothers on the trees at their gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Chun entered Luoyang, he hung the heads of Shilong and his brothers from the trees at their gate.

sentences.zh: 椿父出見，謂曰：「汝與爾硃約為兄弟，今何忍縣其頭於家門？

translations.literal: Chun's father came out to see him and said, "You swore brotherhood with the Erzhu. How can you bear to hang their heads at your own gate?
translations.idiomatic: Chun's father came out and said, "You swore brotherhood with the Erzhu. How can you bear to hang their heads at our gate?

sentences.zh: 寧不愧負天地！」

translations.literal: Are you not ashamed before Heaven and Earth!"
translations.idiomatic: Have you no shame before Heaven and Earth!"

sentences.zh: 椿乃傳世隆等首，並囚度律、天光，送于齊神武。

translations.literal: Chun then sent on the heads of Shilong and the others, imprisoned Dulü and Tianguang, and delivered them to Duke Shenwu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Chun then sent on the heads, imprisoned Dulü and Tianguang, and delivered them to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 及神武入洛，椿謂賀拔勝曰：「今天下事在吾與君，若不先制人，將為人所制。

translations.literal: When Duke Shenwu of Qi entered Luoyang, Chun said to Heba Sheng, "The affairs of the realm now rest with you and me. If we do not strike first and control others, we shall be controlled by others.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Chun told Heba Sheng, "The fate of the realm is in our hands. Unless we strike first, others will strike at us.

sentences.zh: 高歡初至，圖之不難。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan has only just arrived; to plot against him would not be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan has only just arrived; eliminating him would not be hard."

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「彼有心於人，害之不詳。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "He treats people with genuine feeling. To harm him would be inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "He treats people with real goodwill. To harm him would be ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 比數夜與歡同宿，具序往昔之懷，兼荷兄恩意甚多，何苦憚之！」

translations.literal: These past several nights I have lodged with Huan and he has fully recounted our former friendship. I also owe your elder brother a great debt of kindness. Why trouble yourself to fear him!"
translations.idiomatic: I have spent the last several nights with Huan, and he has spoken at length of our old friendship. I also owe your elder brother a great debt. Why be so wary of him!"

sentences.zh: 椿乃止。

translations.literal: Chun thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Chun dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝立，拜椿侍中、儀同開府、城陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was enthroned, Chun was appointed Palace Attendant, Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with the privilege of an independent office, and Duke of Chengyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Chun was made Palace Attendant, Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, and Duke of Chengyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父足亦加開府，子悅太中大夫，同日受拜。

translations.literal: His father Zu was also granted the title of Grand Master with Golden Tally, and his son Yue was made Grand Master of Palace Leisure; all received their appointments on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zu was also granted the title of Grand Master with Golden Tally, and his son Yue was made Grand Master of Palace Leisure; all three were appointed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 當時榮之。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was considered a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 椿自以數反，意常不安，遂密勸孝武帝置閣內都督部曲，又增武直人數百，直閣已下員別數百，皆選天下輕剽以充之。

translations.literal: Because Chun had changed sides several times, he was constantly uneasy in mind and therefore secretly urged Emperor Xiaowu to establish an inner palace guard corps under a commander, to add several hundred martial attendants, and to set aside several hundred posts below the rank of Attendant at the Inner Gate, all filled by selecting the most daring and swift men from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Having changed sides so often, Chun was never at ease and secretly urged Emperor Xiaowu to form an inner palace guard, add several hundred martial attendants, and create several hundred posts below Attendant at the Inner Gate, all filled with the boldest men from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 又說帝數出遊幸，號令部曲，別為行陣，椿自約勒指麾其間。

translations.literal: He also persuaded the emperor to go out frequently on tours, to issue commands to his troops, and to form them into separate battle arrays, with Chun himself restraining and directing them in the midst.
translations.idiomatic: He also persuaded the emperor to go out on frequent tours, drill his troops in separate formations, and command them himself.

sentences.zh: 從此以後，軍謀朝政，一決於椿。

translations.literal: From this time on, military plans and court policy were decided entirely by Chun.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, military and political decisions rested entirely with Chun.

sentences.zh: 又勸帝徵兵，詭稱南討，將以伐齊神武。

translations.literal: He also urged the emperor to levy troops, falsely announcing a southern campaign in order to attack Duke Shenwu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to mobilize troops under the pretense of a southern campaign, intending to strike at Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以椿為前驅大都督。

translations.literal: Chun was made Grand Commander of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was appointed Grand Commander of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 椿因奏請率精騎二千，夜度河，掩其勞弊。

translations.literal: Chun thereupon memorialized requesting to lead two thousand picked horsemen, cross the river by night, and strike the enemy while they were weary and spent.
translations.idiomatic: Chun then asked to lead two thousand elite horsemen across the river by night and strike the enemy while they were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 帝始然之，黃門侍郎楊寬說帝曰：「高歡以臣伐君，何所不至？

translations.literal: The emperor at first approved this. Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates Yang Kuan said to the emperor, "Gao Huan, as a subject attacking his lord—what would he not dare?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first agreed. Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates Yang Kuan told him, "Gao Huan has already risen as a subject against his sovereign—what would he not dare?

sentences.zh: 今假兵於人，恐生他變。

translations.literal: To lend troops to another man now may give rise to some other turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: To lend him troops now may bring some other disaster.

sentences.zh: 今度河，萬一有功，是滅一高歡，復生一高歡矣。」

translations.literal: If he crosses the river now and by chance succeeds, you will have destroyed one Gao Huan only to create another Gao Huan."
translations.idiomatic: If he crosses the river and succeeds, you will have destroyed one Gao Huan only to create another."

sentences.zh: 帝遂敕椿停行。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Chun to halt his march.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Chun to halt.

sentences.zh: 椿歎曰：「頃熒惑入南斗，今上信左右間構，不用吾計，豈天道乎！」

translations.literal: Chun sighed and said, "Recently Mars entered the Southern Dipper. Now the sovereign believes the slanders of those around him and will not use my plan. Is this the will of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Chun sighed, "Mars has just entered the Southern Dipper. The sovereign believes the intrigues around him and will not take my counsel. Is this Heaven's will!"

sentences.zh: 帝勒兵河橋，命椿自洛而東，至武牢。

translations.literal: The emperor marshaled troops at the Yellow River Bridge and ordered Chun to march east from Luoyang as far as Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assembled his forces at the Yellow River Bridge and ordered Chun to march east from Luoyang to Wulao.

sentences.zh: 帝以賈顯智背叛，東師失律，將幸關中。

translations.literal: Because Jia Xianzhi had turned traitor and the eastern army had lost discipline, the emperor was about to move his court to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Xianzhi defected and the eastern army fell apart, the emperor prepared to flee to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使命椿因從入關。

translations.literal: He therefore sent orders for Chun to follow him into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: He sent orders for Chun to accompany him through the pass into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書令，侍中如故，封常山郡公。

translations.literal: Chun was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs while retaining his post as Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Department of State Affairs while keeping his post as Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 歷位司徒、太保，仍尚書令。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister over the Masses and Grand Tutor while still serving as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Minister over the Masses and Grand Tutor while remaining Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時寇難未息，內外戒嚴，唯椿得列威儀，鳴騶清路。

translations.literal: At that time raids and turmoil had not yet ceased and the court and the realm were on alert, yet only Chun was permitted to display full ceremonial escort, with outriders clearing the road.
translations.idiomatic: Though raids and turmoil continued and the realm remained on alert, only Chun was allowed a full ceremonial escort with outriders clearing his path.

sentences.zh: 遷太傅，薨，年四十三。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the post of Grand Tutor and died at the age of forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor and died at the age of forty-three.

sentences.zh: 帝親臨吊，百僚赴哭。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to offer condolences, and the officials all went to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him, and the officials all attended the funeral.

sentences.zh: 詔賜東園秘器，遣尚書、梁郡王景略監護喪事。

translations.literal: An edict granted the funerary regalia of the Eastern Garden and dispatched the Director of the Department of State Affairs, the Prince of Liang Commandery Jinglue, to supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the funerary regalia of the Eastern Garden and sent Director of the Department of State Affairs Prince Jinglue of Liang Commandery to supervise the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、錄尚書、三十州諸軍事、侍中、恆州刺史、常山郡王，諡曰文宣，祭乙太牢。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles of Grand General, Supervisor of the Department of State Affairs, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Thirty Provinces, Palace Attendant, Regional Inspector of Heng Province, and Prince of Changshan Commandery, with the posthumous name Wenxuan, and sacrifices of the second yi grade with the great offering were performed.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand General, Supervisor of the Department of State Affairs, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Thirty Provinces, Palace Attendant, Regional Inspector of Heng Province, and Prince of Changshan Commandery, with the posthumous name Wenxuan and sacrifices of the second yi grade with the great offering.

sentences.zh: 又詔改大將軍，贈大司馬，給轀輬車。

translations.literal: Another edict changed his title from Grand General and posthumously granted him the title of Grand Marshal, with an imperial funeral carriage supplied.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict changed his posthumous rank from Grand General to Grand Marshal and supplied an imperial funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 及葬，車駕臨于渭陽，止紼慟哭。

translations.literal: At the burial the imperial carriage came to Weiyang, halted at the mourning ropes, and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral the emperor came to Weiyang, stopped at the bier ropes, and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗給椿店數區，耕牛三十頭。

translations.literal: The emperor had once granted Chun several shop districts and thirty draft oxen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had once given Chun several shop properties and thirty draft oxen.

sentences.zh: 椿以國難未平，不可與百姓爭利，辭店受牛，日烹一頭，以饗軍士。

translations.literal: Chun held that with the nation's troubles not yet settled he could not compete with the common people for profit. He declined the shops but accepted the oxen, cooking one each day to feast his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Chun argued that while the realm was still in turmoil he could not compete with the people for profit. He declined the shops, took the oxen, and cooked one each day to feed his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及死，家無餘資。

translations.literal: When he died, his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his family had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 有四子：悅、恢、徵、演。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Yue, Hui, Zheng, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Yue, Hui, Zheng, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 演為齊神武所殺，三子入關。

translations.literal: Yan was killed by Duke Shenwu of Qi, and the other three sons entered the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had Yan killed; the other three sons fled west through the pass.

sentences.zh: 徵字士亮，博涉群書，尤精三禮，兼解音律。

translations.literal: Zheng, styled Shiliang, ranged widely through the classics and was especially expert in the Three Rites, while also understanding musical pitch and mode.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, courtesy name Shiliang, was widely read in the classics, especially versed in the Three Rites, and also understood music theory.

sentences.zh: 有至性。

translations.literal: He possessed utmost filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，朝夕共一溢米。

translations.literal: While mourning his father, morning and evening he shared a single yi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he ate only a single yi of rice each day.

sentences.zh: 少以父勳賜爵城陽郡公。

translations.literal: In youth, because of his father's merit, he was granted the title Duke of Chengyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chengyang Commandery on account of his father's merit.

sentences.zh: 大統末，起家通直散騎常侍，稍遷兼太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the end of the Datong era he first entered office as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalier Attendant, and was gradually promoted to concurrent Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Datong era he entered office as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalier Attendant and was gradually promoted to concurrent Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 自魏孝武遷西，雅樂廢缺，徵博采遺逸，稽諸典故，創新改舊，方始備焉。

translations.literal: From the time Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, court music had fallen into ruin and loss. Zheng broadly gathered what had survived, examined the ancient precedents, created the new and revised the old, and only then made it complete.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, court music had fallen into ruin. Zheng gathered surviving materials, consulted ancient precedents, revised old pieces and created new ones, and at last restored the repertoire.

sentences.zh: 又樂有錞於者，近代絕此器，或有自蜀得之，皆莫之識。

translations.literal: There was also in music an instrument called the chunyu. In recent times this instrument had disappeared; when someone obtained one from Shu, no one recognized it.
translations.idiomatic: Music also included an instrument called the chunyu, which had long been lost. When someone obtained one from Shu, no one could identify it.

sentences.zh: 徵見之曰：「此錞於也。」

translations.literal: When Zheng saw it he said, "This is a chunyu."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng saw it and said, "This is a chunyu."

sentences.zh: 眾弗信之，徵遂依干寶《周禮注》，以芒筒捋之。

translations.literal: The crowd did not believe him. Zheng then, following Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou, struck it with a tube of awn grass.
translations.idiomatic: No one believed him. Zheng then followed Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou and struck it with a tube of awn grass.

sentences.zh: 其聲極清，眾乃嘆服。

translations.literal: Its sound was extremely clear, and the crowd then sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The tone was extraordinarily clear, and everyone marveled.

sentences.zh: 徵仍取以合樂焉。

translations.literal: Zheng then took it and incorporated it into the ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng then incorporated it into the court orchestra.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜司樂下大夫，遷司樂中大夫，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，轉內史下大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Office of Music, then promoted to Middle Grand Master of the Office of Music, advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, and transferred to Lower Grand Master of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he became Lower Grand Master of the Office of Music, then Middle Grand Master of the Office of Music, then General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, and finally Lower Grand Master of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，周武帝以徵經有師法，詔令授皇諸子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, Emperor Wu of Zhou, because Zheng's learning had a proper lineage of masters, ordered him to instruct the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe, Emperor Wu of Zhou ordered Zheng to instruct the imperial princes because his scholarship followed a proper lineage.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時為魯公，與諸皇子等咸服青衿，行束脩之禮，受業於徵。

translations.literal: At that time the future Emperor Xuan was Duke of Lu. He and the other imperial princes all wore the blue collar, performed the ceremony of presenting dried meat as tuition, and received instruction from Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Xuan was then Duke of Lu. He and the other princes wore scholars' dress, presented the traditional tuition gift, and studied under Zheng.

sentences.zh: 仍並呼徵為夫子，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: They all also addressed Zheng as Master, to the glory of the Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: They all called Zheng Master, to the envy of other scholars.

sentences.zh: 六年，除司宗中大夫，行內史，仍攝樂部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Middle Grand Master of the Office of Imperial Clan, acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat, while still overseeing the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Middle Grand Master of the Office of Imperial Clan and acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat while still overseeing the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 進封岐國公，尋轉小宗伯。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Qi State and soon transferred to Lesser Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Qi State and soon became Lesser Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 除太子太傅，仍小宗伯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent while retaining the post of Lesser Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent while keeping his post as Lesser Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，遷上大將軍、大宗伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Zheng was transferred to Grand General and Grand Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Zheng was promoted to Grand General and Grand Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時武帝初崩，梓宮在殯，帝意欲速葬，令朝臣議之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu had just died and the coffin was still in mourning hall. The emperor wished to bury him quickly and ordered the court officials to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had just died and his coffin still lay in the mourning hall. Emperor Xuan wished to bury him quickly and ordered the court to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 徵與內史宇文孝伯等，固請依《禮》七月，帝竟不許。

translations.literal: Zheng, together with Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuwen Xiaobo and others, firmly requested burial according to the Rites after seven months, but the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuwen Xiaobo and others firmly urged burial after seven months as the Rites prescribed, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 帝之為太子也，宮尹鄭譯坐不能以正道調護，被謫除名。

translations.literal: When the emperor had been heir apparent, the palace steward Zheng Yi was punished for failing to guide and protect him by the right path and was dismissed and removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan had been heir apparent, palace steward Zheng Yi was dismissed for failing to guide him properly.

sentences.zh: 而帝雅親愛譯。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor had always been personally fond of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor had always been fond of him.

sentences.zh: 至是，拜譯內史中大夫，甚委任之。

translations.literal: At this time Yi was appointed Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Secretariat and greatly entrusted with authority.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yi was appointed Middle Grand Master of the Imperial Secretariat and given great authority.

sentences.zh: 譯乃獻新樂，十二月各一笙，每笙用十六管。

translations.literal: Yi then presented new music: one sheng for each of the twelve months, each sheng using sixteen pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then presented new music: twelve sheng, one for each month, each with sixteen pipes.

sentences.zh: 帝令與徵議之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that it be discussed with Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zheng to review it.

sentences.zh: 徵駁而奏之曰：「《禮》雲，十二律轉相生，聲五具在十六焉，六律十二管，還相為宮。

translations.literal: Zheng refuted it and memorialized, saying, "The Rites state that the twelve pitch standards generate one another in succession, that the five tones are all contained within sixteen, and that six standards and twelve pipes alternately serve as the keynote.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng objected and memorialized, "The Rites teach that the twelve pitch standards generate one another in succession, that the five tones are contained within sixteen pipes, and that six standards and twelve pipes alternate as keynote.

sentences.zh: 然詳一笙十六管，總一百九十二管，既無相生之理，又無還宮之義。

translations.literal: Yet if one examines a single sheng of sixteen pipes, the total of one hundred ninety-two pipes has neither the principle of mutual generation nor the meaning of returning to the keynote.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a single sheng of sixteen pipes means one hundred ninety-two pipes in all, which observe neither mutual generation nor return to the keynote.

sentences.zh: 臣恐鄭聲亂樂，未合于古。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that the music of Zheng will disorder proper music and does not accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this is the decadent music of Zheng corrupting proper music and does not accord with antiquity.

sentences.zh: 夫音樂之起，本于人心，天之應人，有如影響。

translations.literal: Music arises from the human heart, and Heaven's response to humanity is like shadow to form.
translations.idiomatic: Music arises from the human heart, and Heaven responds to humanity as shadow follows form.

sentences.zh: 為善者，天報之以福；

translations.literal: Those who do good, Heaven rewards with blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Those who do good receive Heaven's blessing;

sentences.zh: 為惡者，天譴之以殃。

translations.literal: those who do evil, Heaven punishes with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: those who do evil receive Heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 故舜彈五弦之琴，歌《南風》之詩，而天下化。

translations.literal: Therefore Shun played the five-stringed zither and sang the ode "Southern Breeze," and all under Heaven was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Shun played the five-stringed zither and sang the "Southern Breeze," and the realm was transformed.

sentences.zh: 紂為朝歌、北裏之音，而社稷滅。

translations.literal: Zhou made the music of Chaoge and Beili, and the altars of state were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou indulged in the music of Chaoge and Beili, and his dynasty perished.

sentences.zh: 是知樂也者，和情性，移風俗，動天地，感鬼神，禍福所基，盛衰攸系，安可不慎哉！

translations.literal: From this we know that music harmonizes emotion and nature, transforms customs, moves Heaven and Earth, stirs ghosts and spirits, is the foundation of blessing and calamity, and is bound up with rise and decline—how can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Thus music harmonizes the emotions, transforms customs, moves Heaven and Earth, stirs spirits, and underlies fortune and ruin, rise and fall—how can one not be cautious!

sentences.zh: 案譯之所為，不師古始。

translations.literal: Examining what Yi has done, it does not follow the ancient beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: What Yi proposes does not follow ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 若以月奏一笙，則鐘鼓諸色，各須一十有二。

translations.literal: If one sheng is played for each month, then bells, drums, and the other categories would each likewise require twelve sets.
translations.idiomatic: If one sheng is played each month, bells, drums, and every other instrument would likewise require twelve sets.

sentences.zh: 雅樂之備，已充廟廷，今若益之，于何陳列？

translations.literal: The court music is already complete and fills the temple hall. If more is added now, where will it be displayed?
translations.idiomatic: Court music already fills the temple hall. Where would more instruments be placed?

sentences.zh: 方須更辟階墀，增修廊宇，非急之務，寧可勞人？

translations.literal: One would still need to open new steps and terraces and enlarge the corridors and halls. This is not urgent business—how can one burden the people?
translations.idiomatic: We would need new terraces and enlarged halls. This is not urgent—why burden the people?

sentences.zh: 如謂笙管之外，不須加造，則樂之損益，豈系於笙？

translations.literal: If one says that beyond the sheng pipes nothing further need be made, then does the increase or decrease of music depend on the sheng alone?
translations.idiomatic: If beyond the sheng nothing else need be made, does music's gain or loss depend on the sheng alone?

sentences.zh: 進退無據，竊謂不可。」

translations.literal: Advancing or retreating has no basis. Your servant respectfully holds that this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: The proposal has no coherent basis. I respectfully submit that it cannot be accepted."

sentences.zh: 帝頗納之，且令停譯所獻。

translations.literal: The emperor largely accepted this and also ordered a halt to what Yi had presented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely agreed and ordered Yi's proposal suspended.

sentences.zh: 及武帝山陵回，帝欲作樂，復令議其可不。

translations.literal: When the procession returned from Emperor Wu's tomb mound, the emperor wished to perform music and again ordered discussion of whether this was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: When the procession returned from Emperor Wu's tomb, Xuan wished to perform music and again ordered the court to discuss whether it was permissible.

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「《孝經》云'聞樂不樂。

translations.literal: Zheng said, "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'On hearing music one does not feel joy.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'On hearing music one does not feel joy.

sentences.zh: '聞尚不樂，其況作乎！」

translations.literal: If on hearing one does not feel joy, how much less should one perform it!"
translations.idiomatic: If hearing music brings no joy, how much less should one perform it!"

sentences.zh: 鄭譯曰：「既雲聞樂，明即非無，止可不樂，何容不奏。」

translations.literal: Zheng Yi said, "Since it speaks of hearing music, it clearly does not mean there is none. One need only not feel joy—how can one refuse to perform it?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi replied, "Since it speaks of hearing music, music clearly exists. One need only not feel joy—why refuse to perform it?"

sentences.zh: 帝遂依譯議，譯因此銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon followed Yi's opinion, and Yi therefore bore a grudge against Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Yi's view, and Yi bore a grudge against Zheng.

sentences.zh: 帝后肆行非度，昏慮日甚。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor wantonly acted beyond all measure, and his confused judgment grew worse day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the emperor's conduct grew ever more lawless and his judgment ever more clouded.

sentences.zh: 徵以荷武帝重恩，嘗備位師傅，乃上疏極諫，指陳帝失。

translations.literal: Because Zheng bore the heavy favor of Emperor Wu and had once served as tutor, he submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance, pointing out the emperor's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Emperor Wu's great favor and his own former role as tutor, Zheng submitted a forceful memorial enumerating the emperor's faults.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: It was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 譯因譖之，遂下徵於獄。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon slandered him, and Zheng was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yi slandered him, and Zheng was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 徵懼不免，獄卒張元平哀之，乃以佩刀穿牆，送之出。

translations.literal: Fearing he could not escape death, Zheng was pitied by the prison guard Zhang Yuanping, who bored through the wall with his belt knife and sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, Zheng was helped by prison guard Zhang Yuanping, who bored through the wall with his belt knife and helped him escape.

sentences.zh: 元平被捶拷百數，而無所言。

translations.literal: Yuanping was beaten several hundred times but said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping was beaten hundreds of times but revealed nothing.

sentences.zh: 徵既出，匿於人家，後遇赦得免，然猶坐除名。

translations.literal: After Zheng escaped he hid in a private household. Later he was spared by an amnesty, but was still punished by removal from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng hid in a private home, was later spared by an amnesty, but was still struck from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，例復官爵，除太子太傅，仍詔徵修撰樂書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, Zheng's rank and titles were restored according to precedent. He was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and an edict also ordered him to compile a book on music.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui came to the throne, Zheng's rank and titles were restored. He was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and ordered to compile a treatise on music.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年薨，年五十六。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Kaihuang at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Kaihuang at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 初，隋文帝為大司馬，有外姻喪，徵就第吊之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wen of Sui was Grand Marshal, a relative by marriage died and Zheng went to his residence to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wen was Grand Marshal, a relative by marriage died and Zheng came to offer condolences at his residence.

sentences.zh: 久而不出。

translations.literal: Wen remained inside for a long time without coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Wen kept him waiting a long time without appearing.

sentences.zh: 徵怒，遂弗之待。

translations.literal: Zheng grew angry and would not wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng grew angry and left without waiting.

sentences.zh: 比出候，徵已去矣。

translations.literal: By the time Wen came out to receive him, Zheng had already departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen finally came out to receive him, Zheng was already gone.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝以此常恨之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui always resented him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen never forgave him for this.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔所司諡之曰闇。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered the relevant offices to give him the posthumous name An.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the relevant offices to give him the posthumous name An.

sentences.zh: 子該嗣。

translations.literal: His son Gai succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 徽所撰《樂典》十卷。

translations.literal: Zheng compiled the Music Canon in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng compiled the Music Canon in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 兄恢，散騎常侍，新蔡郡公。

translations.literal: His elder brother Hui was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Xincai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Hui was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Xincai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子政嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 政明悟有器幹，隋開皇中，以軍功授儀同，甚為楊素所禮。

translations.literal: Zheng was intelligent, perceptive, and capable. In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was granted the title of Grand Master with Golden Tally for military merit and was greatly honored by Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was intelligent and capable. In the Kaihuang era he was granted the title of Grand Master with Golden Tally for military merit and was greatly honored by Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 大業中，位尚書兵曹郎，漸見委遇。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he held the post of Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Department of State Affairs and was gradually entrusted with favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he served as Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was gradually given greater trust.

sentences.zh: 玄感兄弟，俱與之交。

translations.literal: The Xuan'gan brothers were all on friendly terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with the Xuan'gan brothers.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，兵部尚書段文振卒，侍郎明雅復以罪廢，帝彌屬意於政。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign, Minister of War Duan Wenzhen died and Vice Director Mingya was again dismissed for a crime. The emperor placed ever greater hopes in Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, Minister of War Duan Wenzhen died and Vice Director Mingya was dismissed for a crime. The emperor placed ever greater hopes in Zheng.

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 稱為幹理。

translations.literal: He was praised for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was praised for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 玄感之反，政與通謀，及玄縱等亡歸，亦政之計。

translations.literal: When Xuan'gan rebelled, Zheng conspired with him, and when Xuanzong and the others fled and returned, that too was Zheng's plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan'gan rebelled, Zheng conspired with him, and when Xuanzong and the others fled home, that too was Zheng's plan.

sentences.zh: 及帝窮玄縱黨與，政亡奔高麗。

translations.literal: When the emperor pursued Xuanzong's associates to the end, Zheng fled and took refuge in Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor hunted down Xuanzong's associates, Zheng fled to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復東征，高麗請和，遂送政。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned east again. Goguryeo sued for peace and sent Zheng back.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor campaigned east again. Goguryeo sued for peace and extradited Zheng.

sentences.zh: 鎖至京師以告廟，左翊衛大將軍宇文述請變常法行刑，帝許之。

translations.literal: He was brought in chains to the capital to announce the matter at the ancestral temple. Left Wing Guard General Yuwen Shu requested that the usual law be altered in carrying out the execution, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought in chains to the capital to report to the ancestral temple. Left Wing Guard General Yuwen Shu asked to alter the usual mode of execution, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 以出金光門，縛之於柱，公卿百僚，並親擊射。

translations.literal: He was taken out through the Golden Light Gate and bound to a pillar. The dukes, ministers, and hundred officials all personally shot at him.
translations.idiomatic: He was taken out through the Golden Light Gate and bound to a pillar. The nobles and officials all shot at him in person.

sentences.zh: 臠其肉，多有啖者，然後烹焚，揚其骨灰。

translations.literal: His flesh was cut into pieces and many ate of it. Then he was boiled and burned, and his ashes were scattered to the winds.
translations.idiomatic: His flesh was cut up and many ate it. Then his body was boiled and burned, and his ashes were scattered.

sentences.zh: 椿弟元壽，性剛毅諒直，武力過人，彎弓兩石，左右馳射。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Yuanshou was firm, resolute, sincere, and upright by nature. His martial strength surpassed others': he could draw a bow of two shi and shoot on horseback to left and right while galloping.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Yuanshou was firm, upright, and exceptionally strong. He could draw a two-shi bow and shoot accurately from horseback at full gallop.

sentences.zh: 歷位吏部尚書，封桑乾縣伯。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Minister of Personnel and was enfeoffed as Baron of Sanggan County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Personnel and was enfeoffed as Baron of Sanggan County.

sentences.zh: 孝武踐阼，進爵為公，除豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, Yuanshou's noble rank was advanced to duke and he was appointed Regional Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Yuanshou was promoted to duke and appointed Regional Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 及車駕西巡，為部下所殺。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured west, he was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved west, his own subordinates killed him.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公，諡曰景莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Duke of Works, with the posthumous name Jingzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Duke of Works, with the posthumous name Jingzhuang.

sentences.zh: 賈顯度，中山無極人也。

translations.literal: Jia Xiandu was a native of Wuji in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xiandu came from Wuji in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 父道監，沃野鎮長史。

translations.literal: His father Daojian was chief clerk of Woye Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daojian had been chief clerk of Woye Garrison.

sentences.zh: 顯度形貌偉壯，有志氣。

translations.literal: Xiandu was imposing and stalwart in appearance and possessed resolution and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiandu was imposing in stature and full of resolve.

sentences.zh: 初為別將，防守薄骨律鎮。

translations.literal: He first served as a separate commander defending Boguli Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a separate commander defending Boguli Garrison.

sentences.zh: 正光末，北鎮擾亂，顯度乃率鎮人浮河而下，達秀容，為爾硃榮所留。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhengguang era the northern garrisons were thrown into turmoil. Xiandu then led the garrison people down the river by boat, reached Xiurong, and was detained by Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengguang era the northern garrisons rebelled. Xiandu led the garrison people downriver by boat to Xiurong, where Erzhu Rong detained them.

sentences.zh: 隨榮破葛榮，封石艾縣公，累遷南袞州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Rong in defeating Ge Rong, was enfeoffed as Duke of Shi'ai County, and was repeatedly promoted to Regional Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Rong in defeating Ge Rong, was enfeoffed as Duke of Shi'ai County, and rose to Regional Inspector of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之死，顯度奔梁。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Xiandu fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Xiandu fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，還朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Putai era he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 後隨爾硃度律等敗于韓陵，與斛斯椿及弟智等先據河橋，誅爾硃氏。

translations.literal: Later, when he followed Erzhu Dulü and the others in defeat at Hanling, he joined Hu Sichun and his younger brother Zhi and the others in seizing the Yellow River Bridge first and executing the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after defeat at Hanling with Erzhu Dulü and the others, he joined Hu Sichun and his younger brother Zhi in seizing the Yellow River Bridge and slaughtering the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初，除尚書左僕射，尋加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、定州大中正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon thereafter was further made General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, and chief arbiter of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, and chief arbiter of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，為雍州刺史、西道大行台。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he became Regional Inspector of Yong Province and Grand March Commissioner of the Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he became Regional Inspector of Yong Province and Grand March Commissioner of the Western Route.

sentences.zh: 親故祖餞于張方橋，顯度執酒曰：「顯智性輕躁，好去就，覆敗吾家，其此人也！」

translations.literal: Relatives and old friends saw him off at Zhangfang Bridge. Xiandu raised his wine and said, "Xianzhi is light and rash by nature, fond of shifting allegiances—he will ruin our house; it is this man!"
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and old friends saw him off at Zhangfang Bridge. Xiandu raised his cup and said, "Xianzhi is flighty and rash, always switching sides—he will destroy our house. This is the man!"

sentences.zh: 武帝入關後，顯智果同于齊神武。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu entered Guan, Xianzhi did indeed side with Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu entered Guan, Xianzhi did in fact join Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝怒，乃賜顯度死。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was enraged and ordered Xiandu to be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was furious and had Xiandu executed.

sentences.zh: 智字顯智，少有膽決，以軍功累遷金紫光祿大夫，封義陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Zhi, with courtesy name Xianzhi, was bold and resolute from youth; through military merit he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Xianzhi, was bold and decisive from youth. Through military merit he rose to Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang County.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃仲遠為徐州刺史，智隸仲遠赴彭城。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhongyuan became Regional Inspector of Xu Province, Zhi was placed under Zhongyuan and went to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhongyuan became Regional Inspector of Xu Province, Zhi served under him and went to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，仲遠舉兵向洛，智不從之。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Zhongyuan raised troops toward Luoyang, but Zhi would not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong died, Zhongyuan marched on Luoyang, but Zhi refused to follow.

sentences.zh: 莊帝聞而善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang heard of this and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang heard of it and commended him.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，還洛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Putai era he returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era he returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 仲遠忿其乖背，議欲殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan resented his defiance and discussed killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan resented his disobedience and considered executing him.

sentences.zh: 智兄顯度先為世隆所厚，世隆為解喻得全。

translations.literal: Zhi's elder brother Xiandu had earlier been favored by Shilong, and Shilong pleaded on his behalf so that he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's elder brother Xiandu had long been favored by Shilong, who interceded and saved him.

sentences.zh: 後進爵為公。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 隨度律等敗于韓陵。

translations.literal: He followed Dulü and the others in defeat at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Dulü and the others to defeat at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 智與顯度、斛斯椿謀誅爾硃氏，顯度據守北中城，令智等入京，禽世隆兄弟。

translations.literal: Zhi joined Xiandu and Hu Sichun in plotting to execute the Erzhu clan. Xiandu held Beizhong City while ordering Zhi and the others to enter the capital and capture Shilong and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi plotted with Xiandu and Hu Sichun to destroy the Erzhu clan. Xiandu held Beizhong City and sent Zhi and the others into the capital to seize Shilong and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初，除開府儀同三司、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was appointed Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, and Regional Inspector of Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was made Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, and Regional Inspector of Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 在州貪縱，甚為人害。

translations.literal: In the province he was greedy and overbearing and greatly harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was greedy and brutal and did great harm to the people.

sentences.zh: 孝武徵還京師，加侍中，除濟州刺史，率眾達東郡，仍停不進。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu recalled him to the capital, added him as Palace Attendant, appointed him Regional Inspector of Ji Province, and though he led his troops to Dong Commandery he still halted and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu recalled him to the capital, made him Palace Attendant, and appointed him Regional Inspector of Ji Province. He led his troops to Dong Commandery but then halted and refused to advance.

sentences.zh: 于長壽津為相州刺史竇泰所破。

translations.literal: At Changshou Ford he was defeated by Dou Tai, Regional Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At Changshou Ford he was defeated by Dou Tai, Regional Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 天平初，赴晉陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianping era he went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 智去就多端，後坐事死。

translations.literal: Zhi was ever shifting in his allegiances; later he was executed on criminal charges.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was forever changing sides; later he was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 樊子鵠，代郡平城人也。

translations.literal: Fan Zihu was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zihu came from Pingcheng in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先荊州蠻酋，徙代。

translations.literal: His ancestors had been chieftains of the Man in Jing Province and moved to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had been Man chieftains in Jing Province before relocating to Dai.

sentences.zh: 父興，平城鎮長史、歸義侯。

translations.literal: His father Xing was chief clerk of Pingcheng Garrison and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing had been chief clerk of Pingcheng Garrison and Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，子鵠貴，乃贈荊州刺史。

translations.literal: During Putai, when Zihu became prominent, his father was posthumously granted Regional Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Putai, after Zihu rose to prominence, his father was posthumously made Regional Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 子鵠逢北鎮擾亂，南至并州，爾硃榮引為都督府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: Zihu encountered the turmoil in the northern garrisons, went south to Bing Province, and Erzhu Rong brought him in as Registrar of the Military Provision Bureau in the Area Commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the northern garrisons' upheaval, Zihu went south to Bing Province, where Erzhu Rong took him on as registrar of the area commander's military provision bureau.

sentences.zh: 使詣京師，靈太后問榮兵勢，子鵠應對稱旨。

translations.literal: He was sent to the capital. Empress Dowager Ling asked about Rong's military strength, and Zihu's replies pleased her.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to the capital, he answered Empress Dowager Ling's questions about Rong's forces to her satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 太后嘉之，除直齊，封南和縣子，令還赴榮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was pleased with him, appointed him to Direct Qi, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Nanhe County, and ordered him to return to join Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased with him, the empress dowager appointed him to Direct Qi, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Nanhe County, and sent him back to Rong.

sentences.zh: 建義初，拜晉州刺史，封永安縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was appointed Regional Inspector of Jin Province and enfeoffed as Baron of Yong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyi he became Regional Inspector of Jin Province and was enfeoffed as Baron of Yong'an County.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，以招納叛蜀，進封中都縣公，又兼尚書行台，政有威信。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, for receiving and settling defectors from Shu, he was advanced to Duke of Zhongdu County; he also concurrently served on the Mobile Office of the Department of State Affairs, and his administration had authority and trust.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he was promoted to Duke of Zhongdu County for receiving Shu defectors, and also headed a mobile office of the Department of State Affairs; his rule commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 尋征授都官尚書、西荊州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Director of the Bureau for Punishments and chief arbiter of Western Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and made Director of the Bureau for Punishments and chief arbiter of Western Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 後兼右僕射，為行台。

translations.literal: Later he also served as Right Vice Director and headed a mobile office.
translations.idiomatic: He later also served as Right Vice Director and as head of a mobile office.

sentences.zh: 進封西陽郡公，尚書如故，假驃騎將軍，率所部為都督。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Xiyang Commandery, retained his directorship, was given acting rank as General of Agile Cavalry, and led his troops as area commander.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Duke of Xiyang Commandery, he kept his ministerial post, was given acting rank as General of Agile Cavalry, and commanded his own troops as area commander.

sentences.zh: 時爾硃榮在晉陽，京師之事，子鵠頗預委寄，故在台閣，征官不解。

translations.literal: At that time Erzhu Rong was in Jinyang; as Zihu had often been entrusted with matters in the capital, even while serving at court his summonses for transfer were repeatedly not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was then in Jinyang. Because Zihu had often been entrusted with capital affairs, his court appointments were repeatedly not released for transfer.

sentences.zh: 後出為殷州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Regional Inspector of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later sent out as Regional Inspector of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 屬歲旱儉，子鵠恐人流亡，乃勒有粟家分濟貧者，並遣人牛易力，多種二麥，州內以此獲安。

translations.literal: In a year of drought and famine Zihu feared the people would flee; he compelled households with grain to share among the poor, sent men and oxen to exchange labor, planted much winter wheat and barley, and the province thereby found peace.
translations.idiomatic: When drought and famine struck, Zihu feared mass flight. He forced grain-rich households to aid the poor, organized labor exchanges of men and oxen, and encouraged heavy planting of winter wheat and barley, and the province was thereby stabilized.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，世隆等遣書招子鵠，子鵠不從。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and the others sent letters recruiting Zihu, but Zihu would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Shilong and the others wrote to recruit Zihu, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 以母在晉陽，啟求移鎮河南。

translations.literal: Because his mother was in Jinyang, he petitioned to transfer his garrison to south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being in Jinyang, he petitioned to move his command south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 莊帝嘉之，除都督、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang approved; he was appointed area commander and Regional Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang approved and made him area commander and Regional Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 行達汲郡，聞爾硃兆入洛，乃度河見仲遠。

translations.literal: Reaching Ji Commandery on the march, he heard Erzhu Zhao had entered Luoyang, crossed the river, and went to see Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching as far as Ji Commandery, he learned Erzhu Zhao had entered Luoyang, crossed the river, and went to Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 仲遠遣鎮汲郡。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan sent him to garrison Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan posted him to garrison Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 兆徵子鵠赴洛，既見，責以乖異之意，奪其部眾，將還晉陽。

translations.literal: Zhao summoned Zihu to Luoyang; when they met he reproached him for disloyalty, stripped him of his troops, and was about to send him back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao summoned Zihu to Luoyang, rebuked him for disloyalty, stripped away his forces, and prepared to send him back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 元曄以為侍中、御史中尉、中軍大都督。

translations.literal: Yuan Ye made him Palace Attendant, Chief Censor, and Grand Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ye appointed him Palace Attendant, Chief Censor, and Grand Commander of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，兼尚書左僕射、東南道大行台，總大都督杜德等追討爾硃仲遠。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he also served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand March Commissioner of the Southeastern Route, overseeing Grand Commander Du De and others in pursuing Erzhu Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he also became Left Vice Director and Grand March Commissioner of the Southeastern Route, directing Grand Commander Du De and others against Erzhu Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 仲遠奔梁，收其兵馬。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan fled to Liang; they gathered his troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan fled to Liang, and they collected his troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 時梁遣元樹入寇，陷據譙城，詔子鵠與德討之。

translations.literal: Then Liang sent Yuan Shu to invade; he seized and held Qiao City. The emperor ordered Zihu and De to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then sent Yuan Shu to invade and seize Qiao City. The court ordered Zihu and De to attack him.

sentences.zh: 樹大敗，奔入城門，遂圍之。

translations.literal: Shu was heavily defeated and fled into the city gate; they then besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was routed and fled inside the gates; they laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 樹請歸南，以地還魏，許之。

translations.literal: Shu asked to return south and restore the territory to Wei; they agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked to withdraw south and return the territory to Wei; they agreed.

sentences.zh: 及樹眾半出，子鵠擊破之，禽樹及梁譙州刺史硃文開。

translations.literal: When half of Shu's force had come out, Zihu attacked and broke them, capturing Shu and Zhu Wenkai, Liang's Regional Inspector of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: When half of Shu's troops had emerged, Zihu struck and routed them, capturing Shu and Zhu Wenkai, Liang's inspector of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 班師，遷吏部尚書，轉尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On returning from the campaign he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and then to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋加驃騎大將軍、開府，典選。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with an independent office and oversaw selections for office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further made General of Agile Cavalry with an independent office and put in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 後除兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Regional Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Regional Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 子鵠先遣腹心，緣曆人間，采察得失。

translations.literal: Zihu first sent trusted agents to travel among the people and observe what was going wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking office, Zihu sent trusted agents through the region to learn what was amiss.

sentences.zh: 及至境，太山太守彭穆參候失儀，子鵠責讓穆，並數其罪狀，穆皆引伏，於是州內震悚。

translations.literal: When he reached the border, Tai Mountain Prefect Peng Mu came to pay respects with improper etiquette. Zihu reproached Mu and listed his offenses one by one; Mu confessed to all, and the whole province quaked.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the border, Tai Mountain Prefect Peng Mu paid his respects with improper ceremony. Zihu rebuked him and enumerated his crimes; Mu confessed to everything, and the whole province trembled.

sentences.zh: 及孝武帝入關，子鵠據城為應，南青州刺史大野拔率眾就子鵠。
