translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guan, Zihu held the city in support; Daye Ba, Regional Inspector of Southern Qing Province, led his troops to join Zihu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guan, Zihu held his city in support, and Daye Ba, Regional Inspector of Southern Qing Province, marched to join him.

sentences.zh: 天平初，齊神武遣儀同三司婁昭等討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Gao Huan sent Masters of Ceremony Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes Lou Zhao and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianping, Gao Huan sent Lou Zhao and other masters of ceremony equal to the three dukes to attack him.

sentences.zh: 城久不拔，昭以水灌城。

translations.literal: The city could not be taken for a long time; Zhao flooded it with water.
translations.idiomatic: The siege dragged on until Zhao flooded the city with water.

sentences.zh: 而大野拔因與相見，令左右斬子鵠以降。

translations.literal: But Daye Ba met with him in person and had his attendants behead Zihu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Daye Ba then met with him in person and had his men behead Zihu to surrender.

sentences.zh: 侯深，神武尖山人也。

translations.literal: Hou Shen was a native of Jianshan in Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shen came from Jianshan in Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 機警有膽略。

translations.literal: He was quick-witted and bold in stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He was sharp-witted and bold in counsel.

sentences.zh: 孝明末年，六鎮饑亂，深隨杜洛周南寇。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xiaoming's reign the six garrisons suffered famine and rebellion; Shen followed Du Luozhou south on raids.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaoming's last years the six garrisons starved and rebelled; Shen followed Du Luozhou on southern raids.

sentences.zh: 後與妻兄念賢，背洛周歸爾硃榮。

translations.literal: Later, together with his wife's brother Nian Xian, he deserted Luozhou and returned to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and his wife's brother Nian Xian deserted Luozhou and went over to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 路中遇寇，身披苫褐。

translations.literal: On the road they met bandits; he wore coarse hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they met bandits; he was dressed in coarse hemp.

sentences.zh: 榮賜其衣帽，厚待之，以為中軍副都督。

translations.literal: Rong gave him cap and robes, treated him generously, and made him deputy area commander of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: Rong gave him proper dress, treated him well, and made him deputy commander of the central army.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，封厭次縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yanci County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, Shen was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yanci County.

sentences.zh: 從榮討葛榮於滏口，戰功尤多。

translations.literal: He followed Rong in attacking Ge Rong at Fu Pass and performed exceptionally in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Rong against Ge Rong at Fu Pass and distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 除燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regional Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regional Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮別帥韓樓、郝長等屯據薊城，榮令深討樓，配眾甚少。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Rong's separate commanders Han Lou and Hao Chang and others were stationed at Ji City. Rong ordered Shen to attack Lou but gave him very few troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong's lieutenants Han Lou and Hao Chang and others held Ji City. Rong ordered Shen to attack Lou but gave him very few men.

sentences.zh: 或以為言，榮曰：「深臨機設變，是其所長，若總大眾，未必能用。」

translations.literal: Some spoke against this. Rong said, "Shen excels at adapting when battle is joined—that is his strength; if he commanded a great host he might not be so effective."
translations.idiomatic: Some objected. Rong said, "Shen's gift is improvisation in battle; put him at the head of a great army and he may not do as well."

sentences.zh: 止給騎七百。

translations.literal: He gave him only seven hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him only seven hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 深遂廣張軍聲，率數百騎深入樓境。

translations.literal: Shen thereupon greatly inflated his army's reputation and led several hundred horsemen deep into Lou's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shen then spread exaggerated reports of his force and led several hundred horsemen deep into Lou's territory.

sentences.zh: 去薊百餘里，遇賊帥陳周馬步萬餘，大破之，虜其卒五千餘人。

translations.literal: About a hundred li from Ji he met the bandit commander Chen Zhou with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry, routed them utterly, and captured more than five thousand of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-odd li from Ji he met the rebel commander Chen Zhou with over ten thousand foot and horse, crushed him, and took more than five thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 尋還其馬仗，縱令入城。

translations.literal: Soon he returned their mounts and weapons and let them enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned their horses and arms and let them enter the city.

sentences.zh: 左右諫，深曰：「我兵少，不可力戰，事須為計以離隙之。」

translations.literal: His attendants remonstrated. Shen said, "We have few troops and cannot fight by main force; we must use stratagem to sow division among them."
translations.idiomatic: His men objected. Shen said, "We are too few to fight head-on; we must use a stratagem to set them against one another."

sentences.zh: 深度其已至，遂率騎夜進，昧旦叩其城門。

translations.literal: Having estimated that they had arrived, he led his cavalry forward by night and at dawn knocked on the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Judging them already inside, he led his horsemen forward by night and at dawn knocked on the city gates.

sentences.zh: 韓樓果疑降卒為內應，遂遁走。

translations.literal: Han Lou indeed suspected the surrendered troops were inside collaborators and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lou indeed suspected the captives were inside collaborators and fled.

sentences.zh: 追禽之。

translations.literal: They pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued and took him.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵為侯，尋為平州刺史，仍鎮范陽。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the rank of marquis; soon he became Regional Inspector of Ping Province and continued to garrison Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he was made a marquis; soon he became Regional Inspector of Ping Province and continued to hold Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮死，太守盧文偉誘深出獵，閉門拒之。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Prefect Lu Wenwei lured Shen out on a hunt and shut the gates to refuse him entry.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong died, Prefect Lu Wenwei lured Shen out hunting and shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 深率部曲屯于郡南，為榮舉哀，勒兵南向。

translations.literal: Shen led his followers to camp south of the commandery, held mourning for Rong, and drove his troops south.
translations.idiomatic: Shen camped his followers south of the commandery, mourned Rong, and marched south.

sentences.zh: 莊帝使東萊王貴平為大使，慰勞燕、薊。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang sent Prince Gui Ping of Donglai as chief envoy to comfort Yan and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang sent Prince Gui Ping of Donglai as envoy to reassure Yan and Ji.

sentences.zh: 乃詐降，貴平信之，遂執貴平自隨。

translations.literal: He then feigned surrender; Gui Ping believed him and Shen thereupon seized Gui Ping and took him along.
translations.idiomatic: He then feigned surrender. Gui Ping believed him, and Shen seized him and took him along.

sentences.zh: 進至中山，行台僕射魏蘭根邀擊之，為深所敗。

translations.literal: Advancing to Zhongshan, Mobile Office Vice Director Wei Langen intercepted him and was defeated by Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Zhongshan, he defeated Mobile Office Vice Director Wei Langen, who had moved to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，授深儀同三司、定州刺史、左軍大都督、漁陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was established on the throne, Shen was granted Master of Ceremony Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, appointed Regional Inspector of Ding Province, Left Army Grand Commander, and Duke of Yuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Shen was made Master of Ceremony Equal to the Three Dukes, Regional Inspector of Ding Province, Left Army Grand Commander, and Duke of Yuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝立，仍加開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, he was further given an independent office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, he was further granted an independent office.

sentences.zh: 後隨爾硃兆拒齊神武于廣阿，兆敗走。

translations.literal: Later he followed Erzhu Zhao in resisting Gao Huan at Guang'a; Zhao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Erzhu Zhao against Gao Huan at Guang'a; Zhao was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 深後從神武破爾硃氏于韓陵。

translations.literal: Later Shen followed Gao Huan in defeating the Erzhu clan at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: Shen later followed Gao Huan in crushing the Erzhu at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，除齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Yongxi he was appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi he was appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝末，深與袞州刺史樊子鵠、青州刺史東萊王貴平使信往來，以相連結。

translations.literal: Late in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Shen exchanged envoys with Fan Zihu, Regional Inspector of Yan Province, and Prince Gui Ping of Donglai, Regional Inspector of Qing Province, linking their interests together.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Shen exchanged messages with Fan Zihu of Yan Province and Prince Gui Ping of Donglai in Qing Province, coordinating their positions.

sentences.zh: 又遣使通誠于神武。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to pledge goodwill to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to declare his goodwill to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 及孝武入關，復懷顧望。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guan he again wavered in indecision.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guan he wavered again.

sentences.zh: 汝陽五暹既除齊州刺史，深不時迎納。

translations.literal: After Wu Xian of Ruyang was appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province, Shen did not promptly receive and install him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xian of Ruyang was appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province, Shen did not promptly welcome him in.

sentences.zh: 城人劉桃符等潛引暹入，據西城。

translations.literal: The townspeople Liu Taofu and others secretly brought Xian in and seized the western quarter of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taofu and others in the city secretly admitted Xian and seized the western quarter.

sentences.zh: 深爭門不克，率騎出奔，妻兒部曲，為暹所虜。

translations.literal: Shen fought for the gates but could not prevail; he led his cavalry out in flight, and his wife, children, followers, and attendants were captured by Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen fought for the gates but failed, fled with his cavalry, and Xian captured his wife, children, and followers.

sentences.zh: 行達廣裏，會承制以深行青州事，齊神武又遺書深曰：「卿勿以部曲輕少，難於東邁。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangli, he happened to receive an acting commission to administer Qing Province in his own name. Gao Huan also sent Shen a letter saying, "Do not think your following too slight and few to make the hard march east.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangli he received an acting commission to govern Qing Province. Gao Huan also wrote to him, "Do not think your following too small for the march east.

sentences.zh: 齊人澆薄，齊州人尚能迎汝陽王，青州人豈不能開門待卿也？」

translations.literal: The people of Qi are fickle and shallow; the people of Qi Province were able to welcome the Prince of Ruyang—can the people of Qing Province not open their gates to await you?"
translations.idiomatic: The Qi people are fickle; Qi Province welcomed the Prince of Ruyang—will Qing Province not open its gates for you?"

sentences.zh: 深乃復還，暹始歸其部曲。

translations.literal: Shen then turned back, and Xian only then returned his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Shen turned back, and only then did Xian return his followers.

sentences.zh: 而貴平自以斛斯椿黨，亦不受代。

translations.literal: But Gui Ping, considering himself an ally of Hu Sichun, likewise refused to yield his post.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Ping, counting himself among Hu Sichun's party, likewise refused to step down.

sentences.zh: 深襲高陽郡，克之，置部曲家累於城中，親率輕騎，夜趣青州，城人執貴平出降。

translations.literal: Shen attacked Gaoyang Commandery, took it, left his followers' families in the city, personally led light cavalry by night toward Qing Province, and the townspeople seized Gui Ping and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shen stormed Gaoyang Commandery, took it, left his followers' families there, and led light cavalry by night toward Qing Province; the townspeople seized Gui Ping and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 深自惟反覆，慮不獲安，遂斬貴平，傳首於鄴，明不同於斛斯椿。

translations.literal: Shen reflected on his own constant shifts and feared he would not find safety; he then beheaded Gui Ping and sent the head to Ye to show clearly that he was unlike Hu Sichun.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his own vacillation, Shen feared he could not remain secure; he beheaded Gui Ping and sent the head to Ye to show he was no Hu Sichun.

sentences.zh: 及子鵠平，詔以封延之為青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zihu was pacified, the emperor ordered Feng Yanzhi to be appointed Regional Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Zihu was subdued, the court appointed Feng Yanzhi Regional Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 深既不獲州任，情又恐懼。

translations.literal: Shen neither obtained the provincial appointment nor could quell his fear.
translations.idiomatic: Shen gained neither the province he sought nor peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 行達廣川，遂劫光州庫軍反。

translations.literal: Having reached Guangchuan, he thereupon seized the Guang Province depot troops and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guangchuan, he seized the Guang Province depot troops and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 遣騎詣平原，執前膠州刺史賈璐，夜襲青州南郭，劫前廷尉卿崔光韶以惑人情，攻掠郡縣。

translations.literal: He sent horsemen to Pingyuan, seized the former Regional Inspector of Jiao Province Jia Lu, raided the southern outskirts of Qing Province by night, seized the former Minister of Justice Cui Guangshao to sway popular sentiment, and attacked and plundered commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He sent riders to Pingyuan, seized the former Regional Inspector of Jiao Province Jia Lu, raided Qing Province's southern suburbs by night, took the former Minister of Justice Cui Guangshao hostage to sway the people, and attacked and plundered commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 其部下督帥叛拒之，遂奔梁。

translations.literal: His subordinate commanders rebelled and resisted him, and he thereupon fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate commanders turned against him, so he fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 達南青州境，為賣漿者斬之，傳首於鄴，家口配沒。

translations.literal: When he reached the southern border of Qing Province, a gruel-seller beheaded him; his head was sent to Ye, and his household was confiscated and enslaved.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the southern border of Qing Province, he was beheaded by a gruel-seller; his head was sent to Ye, and his family was confiscated and enslaved.

sentences.zh: 賀拔允，字可泥，神武尖山人也。

translations.literal: Heba Yun, styled Keni, was a native of Jianshan in Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yun, courtesy name Keni, came from Jianshan in Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 其先與魏氏同出陰山，有如回者，魏初為大莫弗。

translations.literal: His forebears had issued from Yinshan together with the Wei clan; one named Ruhui had been made Grand Mofu at the beginning of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had come from Yinshan together with the Wei ruling house; a forebear named Ruhui had served as Grand Mofu in early Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖爾頭，驍勇絕倫，以良家鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ertou was peerless in valor and daring; as a good household he garrisoned Wuchuan and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ertou was unrivaled in valor; as a reputable family they garrisoned Wuchuan and settled there.

sentences.zh: 獻文時以功賜爵龍城縣男，為本鎮軍主。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xianwen, for merit he was granted the noble rank Baron of Longcheng County and made military commander of the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he was enfeoffed as Baron of Longcheng County for his service and made military commander of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 父度拔，性果毅，襲爵，亦為本鎮軍主。

translations.literal: His father Dubo was resolute and daring by nature; he inherited the noble rank and likewise became military commander of the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dubo was resolute and bold; he inherited the title and also served as military commander of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 正光末，沃野人破六韓拔陵反，懷朔鎮將楊鈞聞度拔名，召補統軍，配以一旅。

translations.literal: Late in the Zhenguang era, the Woye tribesman Poha Han Baling rebelled. Yang Jun, commander of Huaishuo Garrison, heard Dubo's reputation, summoned him to fill a post as commander, and assigned him a brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenguang, the Woye tribesman Poha Han Baling rose in rebellion. Yang Jun, commander of Huaishuo Garrison, heard of Dubo's fame, appointed him commander, and gave him a brigade.

sentences.zh: 其賊偽署王衛可環徒党尤盛，既攻沒武川，又陷懷朔，度拔父子並為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Among the rebels' false appointees, the faction of the self-styled king Wei Kehuai was especially strong; having overrun Wuchuan, they also took Huaishuo, and Dubo and his sons were both captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Of the rebels' puppet officers, the band of the self-styled king Wei Kehuai was especially powerful; after Wuchuan fell they took Huaishuo as well, and Dubo and his sons were captured.

sentences.zh: 度拔乃與周德皇帝合謀，率州裏豪傑珍、念賢、乙弗庫根、尉遲檀等，招義勇，襲殺可環。

translations.literal: Dubo then joined in plotting with Yuwen Gong, styled Emperor Zhou De, and with local notables of the province such as Zhen, Nian Xian, Yifu Kugen, and Yuchi Tan; they recruited volunteers, made a surprise attack, and killed Kehuai.
translations.idiomatic: Dubo then conspired with Yuwen Gong, known as Emperor Zhou De, and with local leaders of the region—Zhen, Nian Xian, Yifu Kugen, and Yuchi Tan—raised volunteers, and in a surprise attack killed Kehuai.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: The court commended this.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised the deed.

sentences.zh: 未及封賞，度拔與鐵勒戰沒。

translations.literal: Before rewards and enfeoffments could be granted, Dubo died in battle against the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Before honors could be granted, Dubo fell fighting the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，追贈度拔肆州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Regional Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era Dubo was posthumously made Regional Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 允便弓馬，頗有膽略。

translations.literal: Yun was skilled with bow and horse and possessed considerable daring.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was adept with bow and horse and had no little courage.

sentences.zh: 初度拔之死，允兄弟俱奔恆州刺史廣陽王深。

translations.literal: When Dubo first died, Yun and his brothers all fled to Prince Shen of Guangyang, Regional Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Dubo's death, Yun and his brothers fled to Prince Shen of Guangyang, Regional Inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 深敗，歸爾硃榮。

translations.literal: When the prince was defeated, they submitted to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was defeated, they joined Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 允父子兄弟並以武藝稱，榮素聞其名，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Yun, his father, and his brothers were all famed for martial skill; Rong had long heard their names and treated them with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, his father, and his brothers were all renowned for martial prowess; Rong had long known their names and treated them with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 建義初，封壽陽縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shouyang County.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shouyang County.

sentences.zh: 永安中，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era his noble rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era his rank was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 魏長廣王立，除開府儀同三司，封燕郡王，兼侍中，使蠕蠕。

translations.literal: When Prince Changguang of Wei was enthroned, Yun was appointed Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, enfeoffed as Prince of Yan Commandery, made concurrent Palace Attendant, and sent on embassy to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Changguang of Wei took the throne, Yun was made Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, enfeoffed as Prince of Yan Commandery, appointed concurrent Palace Attendant, and sent as envoy to the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 還至晉陽，屬神武將出山東，允素知神武非常人，早自結托；

translations.literal: On returning to Jinyang, it happened that Gao Huan was about to march east; Yun had long known that Gao Huan was no ordinary man and had early formed ties with him;
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Jinyang, Gao Huan was about to march east; Yun had long seen that Gao Huan was no ordinary man and had courted him early;

sentences.zh: 神武以其北土之望，尤親禮之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, because of his standing among the northern gentry, treated him with especial courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, valuing his prestige in the north, treated him with particular honor.

sentences.zh: 遂與允出信都，參定大策。

translations.literal: He then went out with Yun from Xindu and helped settle the great design.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Xindu with Yun and helped shape the grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 中興初，轉司徒，領尚書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongxing era he was transferred to Minister of Education and appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhongxing era he was made Minister of Education and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 神武入洛，進爵為王，轉太尉，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, his noble rank was advanced to prince; he was transferred to Grand Marshal and added as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Yun was promoted to prince, made Grand Marshal, and given the added post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武既忌神武，以允弟岳據關中，有重兵，深相委託，潛使來往，當是咸慮允為變。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei already mistrusted Gao Huan; because Yun's younger brother Yue held Guanzhong with a large army, the emperor entrusted him deeply and secretly sent envoys back and forth—at the time all feared that Yun might turn traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei already mistrusted Gao Huan; because Yun's younger brother Yue held Guanzhong with a large force, the emperor relied on him deeply and exchanged secret messages—everyone then feared Yun might change sides.

sentences.zh: 及岳死，孝武又委岳兄勝心腹之寄。

translations.literal: When Yue died, Emperor Xiaowu again placed his trust in Yue's elder brother Sheng as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue's death, Emperor Xiaowu again entrusted himself to Yue's elder brother Sheng.

sentences.zh: 神武重舊，尤全護之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan valued their old ties and especially protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan cherished the old bond and especially shielded him.

sentences.zh: 天平元年，因與神武獵，或告允引弓擬神武，乃置於樓上餓殺之，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping, while hunting with Gao Huan, someone reported that Yun had drawn his bow as though aiming at Gao Huan; he was therefore placed in a tower and starved to death, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianping, while hunting with Gao Huan, someone accused Yun of drawing his bow toward him; he was shut in a tower and starved to death at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 神武親臨哭之，贈太保。

translations.literal: Gao Huan came in person to mourn him and posthumously honored him as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan came in person to weep for him and posthumously made him Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 允三子：世文、世樂、難陀。

translations.literal: Yun had three sons: Shiwen, Shile, and Nantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had three sons: Shiwen, Shile, and Nantuo.

sentences.zh: 興和末，齊神武並召與諸子同學。

translations.literal: Late in the Xinghe era, Gao Huan of Qi summoned them together with his sons to study.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xinghe, Gao Huan summoned them to study alongside his sons.

sentences.zh: 武定中，敕居定州，賜田宅。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era an edict ordered them to reside in Ding Province and granted them fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era they were ordered to live in Ding Province and were granted estates.

sentences.zh: 允弟勝。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother was Sheng.

sentences.zh: 勝字破胡，少有志操，善左右馳射，北邊莫不推其膽略。

translations.literal: Sheng, styled Pohu, had ambition and integrity from youth, was skilled at riding and shooting to left and right, and throughout the northern frontier none failed to admire his daring.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, courtesy name Pohu, was ambitious from youth, skilled at shooting from horseback in either direction, and across the northern frontier none failed to respect his courage.

sentences.zh: 衛可瑰之圍懷朔，勝時亦為軍主，從父度拔鎮守。

translations.literal: When Wei Kehuai besieged Huaishuo, Sheng was then a military commander and followed his uncle Dubo in garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Kehuai besieged Huaishuo, Sheng was serving as military commander under his uncle Dubo's command.

sentences.zh: 既被圍，經年而外援不至，勝乃慷慨白鎮將楊鈞，請告急于大軍。

translations.literal: Once besieged, for a full year outside aid did not arrive; Sheng then spoke boldly to the garrison commander Yang Jun, asking leave to report urgently to the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged for a year without relief, Sheng boldly told the garrison commander Yang Jun that he must carry word to the main forces.

sentences.zh: 鈞許之，乃募勇敢少年，得十餘騎，夜潰圍出。

translations.literal: Jun granted this; he then recruited daring youths and obtained a little more than ten horsemen, and by night broke through the encirclement and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed; Sheng recruited bold youths, gathered a dozen horsemen, and broke out by night.

sentences.zh: 賊追及之，勝曰：「我賀拔破胡也。」

translations.literal: The rebels pursued and caught up; Sheng said, "I am Heba Pohu."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels caught up; Sheng cried, "I am Heba Pohu!"

sentences.zh: 賊不敢逼。

translations.literal: The rebels did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 至朔州，白臨淮王彧以懷朔被圍之急。

translations.literal: He reached Shuozhou and reported to Prince Linhuai Yu the urgency of Huaishuo's siege.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Shuozhou and told Prince Linhuai Yu how desperate Huaishuo's plight was.

sentences.zh: 彧以勝辭義懇至，許以出師，還令報命。

translations.literal: Yu, because Sheng's words were earnest in meaning and sincere in tone, promised to march out, and sent him back to deliver the reply.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Sheng's earnest plea, Yu promised to march and sent him back with the answer.

sentences.zh: 乃復攻圍而入，賊追之，射殺數人。

translations.literal: He then fought his way back through the encirclement; the rebels pursued, and he shot several men dead.
translations.idiomatic: He fought back through the siege; pursued by rebels, he shot several dead.

sentences.zh: 至城下，大呼曰：「賀拔破胡與官軍至矣！」

translations.literal: Reaching the foot of the wall, he shouted loudly, "Heba Pohu and the government army have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: At the wall he shouted, "Heba Pohu and the imperial army are here!"

sentences.zh: 城中納之。

translations.literal: The city admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: The city let him in.

sentences.zh: 鈞復遣勝出覘武川。

translations.literal: Jun again sent Sheng out to reconnoiter Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Sheng out again to scout Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 武川已陷。

translations.literal: Wuchuan had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchuan had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 勝乃馳還報懷朔。

translations.literal: Sheng then galloped back to report to Huaishuo.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng galloped back to report at Huaishuo.

sentences.zh: 懷朔亦潰，勝父子遂為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Huaishuo also collapsed; Sheng and his father were then captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishuo too was lost; Sheng and his father were taken by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尋而襲殺可瑰，眾令勝馳告朔州，未反而度拔已卒。

translations.literal: Before long they made a surprise attack and killed Kehuai; the multitude ordered Sheng to gallop and report to Shuozhou, but before he could return Dubo had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they ambushed and killed Kehuai; the crowd sent Sheng to ride to Shuozhou with the news, but before he returned Dubo was already dead.

sentences.zh: 刺史費穆奇勝才略，厚禮留之，委以兵事。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector Fei Mu marveled at Sheng's talent and strategy, treated him with generous rites and kept him, and entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Fei Mu admired Sheng's ability, honored him lavishly, kept him, and put him in charge of troops.

sentences.zh: 時廣陽王深在五原，為破六韓賊所圍，召勝為軍主。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Shen of Guangyang was at Wuyuan, besieged by Poha Han's rebels; he summoned Sheng as military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen of Guangyang was then at Wuyuan, besieged by Poha Han's rebels, and made Sheng his military commander.

sentences.zh: 以功拜統軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made commander.

sentences.zh: 又隸僕射元纂鎮恆州。

translations.literal: He was again attached to Vice Director Yuan Zuan, who garrisoned Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He then served under Vice Director Yuan Zuan at Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 時有鮮于河胡擁朔州流人南下為寇，恆州城人應之。

translations.literal: At that time Xianyu Hehu led displaced people of Shuozhou southward as raiders, and the people of Heng Province city responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Hehu then led Shuozhou refugees south to plunder, and the townspeople of Heng Province rose in support.

sentences.zh: 勝與兄允弟岳相失，勝南投肆州，允、嶽投爾硃榮。

translations.literal: Sheng became separated from his elder brother Yun and younger brother Yue; Sheng fled south to Sizhou, while Yun and Yue submitted to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng lost contact with his brothers Yun and Yue; he fled south to Sizhou while Yun and Yue joined Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮與肆州刺史尉慶賓構隙，引嶽攻肆州，陷。

translations.literal: Rong had a rift with Regional Inspector of Sizhou Wei Qingbin; he brought in Yue to attack Sizhou, and it fell.
translations.idiomatic: Rong quarreled with Sizhou's Regional Inspector Wei Qingbin and brought in Yue to attack the province, which fell.

sentences.zh: 榮得勝，大悅曰：「吾得卿兄弟，天下不足定。」

translations.literal: Rong obtained Sheng and was greatly pleased, saying, "With you and your brothers, pacifying the realm would not be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Rong gained Sheng and exclaimed, "With you brothers, conquering the realm would be easy."

sentences.zh: 勝兄弟三人，遂委質事榮。

translations.literal: The three brothers of the Sheng clan thereupon pledged themselves and served Rong.
translations.idiomatic: All three brothers then pledged themselves to Rong.

sentences.zh: 時杜洛周據幽、定，葛榮據冀、瀛。

translations.literal: At that time Du Luozhou held You and Ding, and Ge Rong held Ji and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luozhou held You and Ding; Ge Rong held Ji and Ying.

sentences.zh: 榮謂勝曰：「並陘險要，我之東門，欲屈君鎮之，如何？」

translations.literal: Rong said to Sheng, "Bingxing Pass is strategically vital—the eastern gate of my domain. I wish to ask you to garrison it; what do you say?
translations.idiomatic: Rong told Sheng, "Bingxing Pass is the key to my eastern frontier. I would like you to hold it—will you?

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「是所願也。」

translations.literal: Sheng said, "That is what I desire."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "That is exactly what I wish."

sentences.zh: 榮乃表勝鎮井陘，以所乘大馬並銀鞍遺之。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon memorialized that Sheng should garrison Jingxing, and gave him the great horse he himself rode together with a silver saddle.
translations.idiomatic: Rong memorialized that Sheng garrison Jingxing and gave him his own great horse with a silver saddle.

sentences.zh: 及榮入洛，以預定策立孝莊帝功，封易陽縣伯。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, for his merit in the plan to enthrone Emperor Zhuang he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang, Sheng was enfeoffed Baron of Yiyang County for helping enthrone Emperor Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 後元天穆北征葛榮，大破之。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Tianmu campaigned north against Ge Rong and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Tianmu marched north against Ge Rong and routed him.

sentences.zh: 時杜洛周餘燼韓樓在薊城結聚，以勝為大都督，鎮中山，樓讋勝威名，竟不敢南寇。

translations.literal: At that time Han Lou, remnant of Du Luozhou, gathered at Ji city; Sheng was made Grand Commander and garrisoned Zhongshan; Lou feared Sheng's renown and in the end did not dare raid south.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lou, last remnant of Du Luozhou, gathered at Ji; Sheng was made Grand Commander at Zhongshan, and Lou, fearing his name, never dared march south.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛陽，榮徵勝，使與爾硃兆自硤石度，大破顥軍，禽其子冠受，遂前驅入洛。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Rong summoned Sheng and had him, together with Erzhu Zhao, cross by way of the Stone Ford, inflict a great defeat on Hao's army, capture his son Guanshou, and then advance as vanguard into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Rong recalled Sheng; with Erzhu Zhao he crossed at the Stone Ford, crushed Hao's army, captured his son Guanshou, and drove ahead into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 進爵真定縣公。

translations.literal: His noble rank was advanced to Duke of Zhending County.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to Duke of Zhending County.

sentences.zh: 及榮死，勝與田怡等奔赴榮第，時宮殿之門未加嚴防，怡等議即攻門。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Sheng rushed with Tian Yi and others to Rong's residence; at that time the palace gates had not yet been strictly guarded, and Yi and the others proposed to attack the gates at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Sheng ran with Tian Yi and others to Rong's mansion; the palace gates were not yet heavily guarded, and Yi urged an immediate assault.

sentences.zh: 勝止之曰：「天子既行大事，必當更有奇謀，吾眾旅不多，何輕爾！」

translations.literal: Sheng stopped them, saying, "The Son of Heaven has already carried out a great act; he is sure to have further stratagems. Our force is small—how can we be so rash!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng stopped them: "The emperor has already struck; he surely has more in mind. We are few—how can we be so reckless!"

sentences.zh: 怡乃止。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yi held back.

sentences.zh: 及世隆夜走，勝隨至河橋。

translations.literal: When Shilong fled by night, Sheng followed him to the Heqiao Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilong fled by night, Sheng followed to Heqiao Bridge.

sentences.zh: 勝以為臣無仇君之義，遂勒所部還都。

translations.literal: Sheng held that as a subject he owed no enmity toward his sovereign, and therefore led his troops back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng held that a subject owes no feud against his sovereign and led his men back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 莊帝大悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 仲遠逼東郡，詔以本官假驃騎大將軍、東征都督，率騎一千，會鄭先護討之，為先護所疑，置之營外，人馬未得休息。

translations.literal: When Zhongyuan pressed Dong Commandery, an edict appointed Sheng in his original office, acting General of Agile Cavalry, Eastern Campaign Commander-in-Chief, leading a thousand horsemen to join Zheng Xianhu in attacking him; Xianhu suspected him and kept him outside the camp, so that men and horses could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhongyuan threatened Dong Commandery, Sheng was made acting General of Agile Cavalry and Eastern Campaign Commander with a thousand horsemen to join Zheng Xianhu; Xianhu distrusted him, kept him outside the camp, and gave his men no rest.

sentences.zh: 俄而仲遠兵至，與戰不利，降之。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongyuan's troops arrived; the battle went badly and he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhongyuan's army arrived; defeated, Sheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復與爾硃氏同謀立節閔帝，以功拜右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He again joined the Erzhu clan in plotting to enthrone Emperor Jiemin, and for merit was appointed General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He again conspired with the Erzhu to enthrone Emperor Jiemin and was made General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃氏將討齊神武，勝時從爾硃度律。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan was about to campaign against Gao Huan, Sheng was then following Erzhu Dulü.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu prepared to march against Gao Huan, Sheng was with Erzhu Dulü.

sentences.zh: 度律與兆不平。

translations.literal: Dulü and Zhao were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü and Zhao were estranged.

sentences.zh: 勝以臨敵構隙，取敗之道，乃與斛斯椿詣兆營和之，反為兆所執。

translations.literal: Sheng held that to breed discord on the eve of battle was the way to defeat; he therefore went with Chun to Zhao's camp to make peace, but was instead seized by Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng judged that quarreling before battle invited defeat; he went with Chun to Zhao's camp to reconcile them, but Zhao seized him instead.

sentences.zh: 度律大懼，引軍還。

translations.literal: Dulü was greatly afraid and led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü was terrified and withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 兆將斬勝，數之曰：「爾殺可環，罪一也；

translations.literal: Zhao was about to execute Sheng and enumerated his crimes, saying, "You killed Kehuai—crime one;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was about to kill Sheng and listed his offenses: "You killed Kehuai—that is the first crime;

sentences.zh: 天柱薨後，不與世隆等俱來而東征仲遠，罪二也。

translations.literal: after the Pillar of Heaven's death you did not come east with Shilong and the others but instead campaigned east against Zhongyuan—crime two.
translations.idiomatic: after the Pillar of Heaven died you did not march east with Shilong but campaigned against Zhongyuan—that is the second.

sentences.zh: 我欲殺爾久矣！」

translations.literal: I have long wished to kill you!
translations.idiomatic: I have wanted you dead for a long time!

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「可環作逆，勝父子誅之，其功不小，反以為罪。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Kehuai rose in rebellion; Sheng and his father killed him—the merit was no small thing, yet you call it a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "Kehuai rebelled; my father and I killed him—a great service, yet you call it a crime.

sentences.zh: 天柱被戮，以君誅臣，勝甯負王，不負朝廷。

translations.literal: When the Pillar of Heaven was slain, it was a subject punishing his lord; Sheng would rather wrong the king than wrong the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pillar of Heaven was killed, a subject struck down his lord; I would rather wrong the king than wrong the throne.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，生死在王。

translations.literal: As for today's affair, life and death rest with Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: As for today, my life is in your hands.

sentences.zh: 但去賊密邇，內構嫌隙，自古迄今，未有不破亡者。

translations.literal: But with the enemy close at hand and dissension bred within, from antiquity to the present none have failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with the foe upon you and strife within, none from antiquity to today have escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 勝不憚死，恐王失策。」

translations.literal: Sheng does not fear death, but fears that Your Highness will lose the right course."
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear death, but I fear you will lose your way."

sentences.zh: 兆乃舍之。

translations.literal: Zhao thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao spared him.

sentences.zh: 勝既免，行百餘里，方追及度律。

translations.literal: After Sheng was released, he had gone more than a hundred li before he at last caught up with Dulü.
translations.idiomatic: Freed, Sheng rode more than a hundred li before he overtook Dulü.

sentences.zh: 齊神武既克相州，兵威漸盛，於是兆及天光、仲遠、度律等眾十餘萬陣于韓陵。

translations.literal: After Gao Huan had taken Xiang Province his military prestige gradually grew; thereupon Zhao together with Tianguang, Zhongyuan, Dulü, and others arrayed more than a hundred thousand men at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Huan took Xiangzhou his power grew; Zhao, Tianguang, Zhongyuan, Dulü, and others then drew up more than a hundred thousand men at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 兆率鐵騎陷陣，出齊神武后，將乘其背而擊之。

translations.literal: Zhao led iron cavalry in breaking the line, passed behind Gao Huan, and was about to strike him from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao led iron cavalry through the line, circled behind Gao Huan, and was poised to strike his rear.

sentences.zh: 度律惡兆之驍悍，懼其陵己，勒兵不進。

translations.literal: Dulü disliked Zhao's ferocity and feared he would dominate him, and therefore held his troops and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü resented Zhao's fierceness, feared being overshadowed, and held his men back.

sentences.zh: 勝以其攜貳，遂以麾下降齊神武。

translations.literal: Sheng, because of this divided loyalty, thereupon lowered his banner and surrendered to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this wavering, Sheng lowered his standard and went over to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 度律軍以此先退，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Dulü's army for this reason retreated first, and they were thereupon greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Dulü's wing withdrew first, and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，以勝為領軍將軍，尋除侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made General of the Palace Guard, and soon thereafter appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was made General of the Palace Guard, then Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝將圖齊神武，以勝弟岳擁眾關西，欲廣其勢援，乃拜都督、荊州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、南道大行台、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was about to plot against Gao Huan; because Sheng's younger brother Yue held a large force in Guanzhong, he wished to broaden his power as support, and therefore appointed him Commander-in-Chief, Regional Inspector of Jing Province, General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, Grand Branch Censorate of the Southern Route, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu planned to move against Gao Huan; because Sheng's younger brother Yue commanded a large force in Guanzhong, he sought to strengthen that pillar and appointed Sheng Commander-in-Chief, Regional Inspector of Jing Province, General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office, Grand Branch Censorate of the Southern Route, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 勝多所克捷，沔北蕩為丘墟。

translations.literal: Sheng won many victories, and north of the Mian River the land was swept into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng won victory after victory, and the country north of the Mian was laid waste.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝敕其子雍州刺史續曰：「賀拔勝北間驍將，爾宜慎之，勿與爭鋒。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang charged his son, Regional Inspector of Yong Province Xu, saying, "Heba Sheng is a fierce general of the north; you should be wary of him and not contend for the edge."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang instructed his son Xu, Regional Inspector of Yong Province: "Heba Sheng is a ferocious northern commander—be careful; do not meet him head-on."

sentences.zh: 續遂城守不敢出。

translations.literal: Xu thereupon held the city and did not dare sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: Xu then shut himself in the city and dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 尋進位尚書令，進爵琅邪郡公。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he was promoted to Director of the Department of State Affairs and advanced in rank to Duke of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Director of the Department of State Affairs and ennobled as Duke of Langye.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武與孝武帝有隙，詔勝引兵赴洛，至廣州，猶豫未進，而帝已入關。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan and Emperor Xiaowu fell out, an edict ordered Sheng to lead troops to Luoyang; he reached Guangzhou, hesitated and did not advance, and the emperor had already entered Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan and Emperor Xiaowu quarreled, Sheng was ordered to march on Luoyang; at Guangzhou he lingered without advancing, and the emperor had already fled into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 勝還軍南陽，遣右丞楊休之奉表入關，又令府長史元穎行州事，勝自率所部，將西赴關中。

translations.literal: Sheng withdrew his army to Nanyang, sent Right Assistant Director Yang Xiuzhi to present a memorial and enter Guanzhong, and ordered the chief clerk of his headquarters Yuan Ying to administer the province; Sheng himself led his troops, intending to go west to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng pulled back to Nanyang, sent Right Assistant Director Yang Xiuzhi with a memorial into Guanzhong, put his chief clerk Yuan Ying in charge of the province, and himself led his men west toward Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 進至浙陽，詔授勝太保、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Advancing to Zheyang, he was by edict made Grand Guardian and put in charge of recording the affairs of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zheyang, an edict made him Grand Guardian and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 聞齊神武已平潼關，禽毛鴻賓，勝乃還荊州。

translations.literal: Hearing that Gao Huan had already pacified Tong Pass and captured Mao Hongbin, Sheng thereupon returned to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Gao Huan had taken Tong Pass and captured Mao Hongbin, Sheng turned back to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 州人鄧誕執元穎，引齊師。

translations.literal: A man of the province, Deng Dan, seized Yuan Ying and brought in the Qi army.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Dan of the province seized Yuan Ying and ushered in the Qi forces.

sentences.zh: 時齊神武已遣行台侯景、大都督高敖曹赴之，勝敗，中流矢，奔梁。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Huan had already sent Branch Censor Hou Jing and Grand Commander Gao Aocao to the scene; Sheng was defeated, struck by a stray arrow, and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had already dispatched Branch Censor Hou Jing and Grand Commander Gao Aocao; Sheng was beaten, wounded by a stray arrow, and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 在南三年，梁武帝遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: In the south for three years, Emperor Wu of Liang treated him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: For three years in the south Emperor Wu of Liang treated him with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 勝乞師北討齊神武，既不果，乃求還。

translations.literal: Sheng begged troops to march north and attack Gao Huan; when this failed, he asked to return.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng asked for an army to strike north at Gao Huan; denied, he sought to go home.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝許之，親餞於南苑。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang granted it and personally gave him a farewell feast in the Southern Park.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu agreed and personally saw him off at the Southern Park.

sentences.zh: 勝自是之後，每執弓矢，見鳥獸南向者，皆不射之，以申懷德之意。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever Sheng took bow and arrow in hand, if he saw birds or beasts facing south he would not shoot them, to express his gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever he hunted, he would not shoot any bird or beast facing south—to show his gratitude to Liang.

sentences.zh: 既至長安，詣闕謝罪。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, he went to the palace to confess his fault.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chang'an he presented himself at court to answer for his conduct.

sentences.zh: 魏帝握勝手，噓欷久之，曰：「初平西徙，永嘉南度，漢、晉皆爾。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor took Sheng's hand and sighed long, saying, "At the beginning of the Jianping era the court moved west; at the Yongjia era it crossed south—the Han and Jin were alike in this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor clasped Sheng's hand and wept a long while. "When Jianping drove the court west and Yongjia drove it south, Han and Jin alike knew such days,

sentences.zh: 事乃關天，非公之咎也。」

translations.literal: The affair concerns Heaven itself—it is not your fault."
translations.idiomatic: this was Heaven's doing, not your fault."

sentences.zh: 乃授太師。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He then made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 從周文帝禽竇泰于小關。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wen of Zhou, he captured Dou Tai at Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Wen of Zhou he captured Dou Tai at Xiaoguan.

sentences.zh: 攻弘農。

translations.literal: He attacked Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 下河北，禽郡守孫晏。

translations.literal: He took Hebei and captured the commandery administrator Sun Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Hebei and took the prefect Sun Yan.

sentences.zh: 摧破東魏軍于沙苑，奔追至河上。

translations.literal: He shattered the Eastern Wei army at Shayuan and pursued the fugitives to the river.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the Eastern Wei army at Shayuan and chased the rout to the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 仍與李弼別攻河東，略定汾、絳。

translations.literal: He then with Li Bi attacked Hedong on a separate front and broadly pacified Fen and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Bi he then struck Hedong on a separate front and brought Fen and Jiang under control.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，勝大破東魏軍，周文令勝收其降卒而還。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao, Sheng inflicted a great defeat on the Eastern Wei army; Emperor Wen ordered Sheng to gather the surrendered troops and return.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao Sheng routed the Eastern Wei army; Emperor Wen had him gather the prisoners and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武率眾攻玉壁，勝以前軍大都督從周文。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan led a host to attack Yubi, Sheng followed Emperor Wen as Grand Commander of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan besieged Yubi, Sheng followed Emperor Wen as commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 見齊武旗鼓，識之，乃募敢勇三千人，配勝以犯其軍。

translations.literal: Seeing the banners and drums of the Qi martial lord, he recognized them and thereupon recruited three thousand daredevils and assigned them to Sheng to strike the enemy army.
translations.idiomatic: He spotted Gao Huan's banners, recognized them, raised three thousand daredevils, and gave them to Sheng to hit the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 勝適與神武遇，連叱而字之曰：「賀六渾，賀拔破胡必殺汝也！」

translations.literal: Sheng happened to meet Shenwu, and shouting again and again called him by his childhood name, saying, "He Liu hun—Heba Pohu will surely kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ran straight into Gao Huan and, shouting his childhood name, cried, "He Liu hun—Heba Pohu will kill you yet!"

sentences.zh: 時勝持槊追神武數里，刃垂及之，神武汗流，氣殆盡。

translations.literal: At that time Sheng, spear in hand, pursued Shenwu for several li; the blade almost reached him—Shenwu sweated profusely and was nearly spent.
translations.idiomatic: With spear in hand he chased Gao Huan for miles; the point nearly found him—Gao Huan ran drenched in sweat, his breath almost gone.

sentences.zh: 會勝馬為流矢所中，死。

translations.literal: But Sheng's horse was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then a stray arrow killed Sheng's horse.

sentences.zh: 比副騎至，神武已逸去。

translations.literal: By the time his escort riders arrived, Shenwu had already escaped.
translations.idiomatic: By the time his escort caught up, Gao Huan was gone.

sentences.zh: 勝歎曰：「今日之事，吾不執弓矢者，天也！」

translations.literal: Sheng sighed and said, "As for today's affair—that I could not keep bow and arrow in hand is Heaven's doing!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sighed, "Today I could not keep my bow in play—that was Heaven's will!"

sentences.zh: 是歲，勝諸子在東者，皆為神武所害。

translations.literal: That year, all of Sheng's sons who were in the east were killed by Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gao Huan killed every son of Sheng still in the east.

sentences.zh: 勝憤恨，因動氣疾，大統十年，薨於位。

translations.literal: Sheng, bitter with resentment, thereby suffered a disorder of the vital breath; in the tenth year of Datong he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wrath and grief brought on a wasting illness; in the tenth year of Datong he died in office.

sentences.zh: 臨終，手書與周文曰：「勝萬里杖策，歸身闕庭，冀望與公掃除逋寇。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he wrote by hand to Emperor Wen, saying, "Sheng, staff in hand for ten thousand li, returned his person to the imperial court, hoping with Your Lordship to sweep away the fleeing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he wrote to Emperor Wen: "I rode ten thousand li home to your court, hoping we might together scourge the remnant foe.

sentences.zh: 不幸殞斃，微志不申。

translations.literal: Unhappily I have perished and fallen; my slight ambition was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Instead I die here, my small wish unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 若死而有知，猶望魂飛賊庭，以報恩遇耳。」

translations.literal: If in death there is awareness, I still hope my soul may fly to the rebels' court to repay your gracious treatment."
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have knowledge, I would still send my soul to the enemy camp to repay your kindness."

sentences.zh: 周文覽書，流涕久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen read the letter and wept for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen read it and wept a long while.

sentences.zh: 勝長於喪亂之中，尤工武藝，走馬射飛鳥，十中其五六。

translations.literal: Sheng grew up amid turmoil and was especially skilled in martial arts; riding at a gallop he shot flying birds and hit five or six of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in chaos, he excelled in arms; galloping, he could bring down five or six birds in ten shots.

sentences.zh: 周文每云：「諸將對敵，神色皆動，唯賀拔公臨陣如平常，真大勇也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen often said, "When the generals face the enemy their expressions all change—only Lord Heba is in battle as in ordinary times; that is true great courage."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen often said, "Other generals change color in battle—only Lord Heba is as calm as at home; that is true courage."

sentences.zh: 自居重任，始愛墳籍，乃招引文儒，討論義理。

translations.literal: Once he bore heavy responsibility he began to love the classics of the tombs and mounds, and thereupon invited literary scholars to discuss principle and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Once burdened with high office he took up the classics, gathered literati, and debated doctrine.

sentences.zh: 性又通率，重義輕財，身死之日，唯有隨身兵仗及書千卷而已。

translations.literal: His nature was also open and direct; he valued righteousness and held wealth light; on the day of his death he had only the arms he carried on his person and a thousand scrolls of books, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Open and plain by nature, he prized honor over wealth; when he died he left only his weapons and a thousand books.

sentences.zh: 初，勝至關中，自以年位素重，見周文不拜。

translations.literal: At first, when Sheng came to Guanzhong, considering that his years and rank had long been eminent, he did not bow on seeing Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng first reached Guanzhong, he thought his years and rank entitled him and did not bow to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 尋而自悔，周文亦有望焉。

translations.literal: Soon he regretted it himself, and Emperor Wen also had hopes for him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it; Emperor Wen, too, had hopes for him.

sentences.zh: 後從宴昆明池，時有雙鳧游池中，周文授弓矢於勝曰：「不見公射久矣，請以為歡。」

translations.literal: Later, attending a banquet at Kunming Pool, when a pair of wild ducks were swimming in the pool, Emperor Wen handed bow and arrows to Sheng and said, "It has been long since we have seen Your Lordship shoot—pray make it our pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a feast on Kunming Pool, a pair of mandarin ducks swam by; Emperor Wen handed Sheng bow and arrows. "We have not seen you shoot in too long—gratify us."

sentences.zh: 勝射之，一發俱中。

translations.literal: Sheng shot them; with one release he hit both.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng loosed once and dropped both.

sentences.zh: 因拜曰：「使勝得奉神武，以討不庭，皆如此也。」

translations.literal: He thereupon bowed and said, "If Sheng could serve Shenwu and punish the recalcitrant, it would all be like this."
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and said, "Had I served Gao Huan and marched against the rebellious, every shot would have been so."

sentences.zh: 周文悅，因是恩禮日重，勝亦盡誠推奉焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was pleased; from this his gracious treatment grew daily heavier, and Sheng also devoted himself utterly in service.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was pleased; from then on favor deepened daily, and Sheng gave himself wholly to his service.

sentences.zh: 贈太宰、錄尚書事，諡曰貞獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Steward and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs; his posthumous title was Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Steward and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, with the temple name Zhenxian.

sentences.zh: 明帝二年，以勝配饗文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdi he was paired to receive sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdi he was given a place in sacrifices at Emperor Wen's temple.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟岳子仲華嗣。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother Yue's son Zhonghua was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; Yue's son Zhonghua succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 位開府儀同三司，襲爵琅邪公。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office and inherited the title Duke of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master with Golden Tally and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes with an independent office and inherited the dukedom of Langye.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位江陵總管。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he was made Commander-in-Chief of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daxiang he became Commander-in-Chief of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 勝弟岳。

translations.literal: Sheng's younger brother Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's younger brother Yue.

sentences.zh: 嶽字阿斗泥，少有大志，愛施好士。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Adouni, in youth had great ambition, loved to give and delighted in scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, courtesy name Adouni, was ambitious from youth, generous, and fond of men of talent.

sentences.zh: 初為太學生。

translations.literal: At first he was a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 及長，能左右馳射，驍果絕人。

translations.literal: When grown, he could shoot to left and right while galloping; his valor and daring were unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he could shoot from the saddle to either hand; his daring was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 不讀兵書，而暗與之合，識者咸異之。

translations.literal: He did not read books of war, yet tacitly accorded with them; those who knew him were all struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: He never read military manuals, yet his instincts matched them—those who knew him marveled.

sentences.zh: 與父兄赴援懷朔，賊王衛可環在城西三百餘步，嶽乘城射之，箭中環臂，賊大駭。

translations.literal: With his father and elder brother he went to relieve Huaishuo; the rebel Wang Weikehuai was more than three hundred paces west of the city wall; Yue mounted the wall and shot him—the arrow struck Kehuai's arm, and the rebels were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: With his father and brother he relieved Huaishuo; the rebel Wang Weikehuai stood three hundred paces west of the wall; Yue shot from the ramparts and hit Kehuai's arm—the rebels panicked.

sentences.zh: 後廣陽王深以為帳內軍主，與兄勝俱鎮恆州。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Guangyang Shen made him commander of the inner guard of his tent, and together with his elder brother Sheng he jointly garrisoned Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangyang Shen later made him commander of his personal guard; he and Sheng garrisoned Heng Province together.

sentences.zh: 州陷，投爾硃榮，榮以為都督。

translations.literal: When the province fell, he submitted to Erzhu Rong; Rong made him a commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the province fell he joined Erzhu Rong, who made him a commander.

sentences.zh: 每帳下與計事，多與榮意合。

translations.literal: Whenever he discussed affairs under the tent with Rong, his views mostly accorded with Rong's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In council under Rong's tent his views usually matched Rong's own.

sentences.zh: 榮與元天穆謀入匡朝廷，問計于嶽。

translations.literal: Rong and Yuan Tianmu plotted to enter the capital and restore the court, and asked Yue for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong and Yuan Tianmu plotted to march on the capital and restore the throne, they asked Yue's counsel.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「夫非常之事，必俟非常之人。

translations.literal: Yue said, "For an extraordinary affair one must await an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "An extraordinary deed demands an extraordinary man.

sentences.zh: 將軍士馬精強，位望隆重，若首舉義旗，伐叛匡救，何往不克，何向不摧！

translations.literal: General, your soldiers and horses are keen and strong, your position and renown weighty—if you first raise the banner of righteousness, punish rebellion and rescue the realm, where would you not conquer, in what direction would you not break through!
translations.idiomatic: Your troops are elite, your standing supreme—raise the righteous standard first, punish rebels and save the throne, and what could withstand you?

sentences.zh: 古人云：'朝謀不及夕，言發不俟駕。

translations.literal: The ancients said, "Plans made in the morning do not last till evening; words spoken need not wait for the carriage to be yoked.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'Plans made at dawn may not survive till dusk; words once spoken need not wait for the chariot.'

sentences.zh: '此之謂矣。」

translations.literal: This is what they meant."
translations.idiomatic: That is the sense."

sentences.zh: 榮與天穆相顧良久，曰：「卿此言，真丈夫之論也。」

translations.literal: Rong and Tianmu looked at each other a long while and said, "Your words, sir, are truly the talk of a great man."
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Tianmu exchanged a long look and said, "That is a man's talk indeed."

sentences.zh: 未幾，孝明帝暴崩，榮疑有故，乃舉兵赴洛。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Xiaoming died suddenly; Rong suspected foul play and thereupon raised troops and marched on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Xiaoming died suddenly; suspecting foul play, Rong marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 配嶽甲卒二千為先驅。

translations.literal: He assigned Yue two thousand armored soldiers as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Yue two thousand armored men as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至河陰，榮既殺朝士，因欲稱帝，疑未能決。

translations.literal: Reaching Heyin, Rong having already killed the court officials, then wished to declare himself emperor but hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin, after slaughtering the courtiers, Rong wished to take the throne himself but could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 岳乃從容致諫，榮尋亦自悟，乃尊立孝莊。

translations.literal: Yue thereupon calmly offered remonstrance; Rong soon came to his senses as well and thereupon honored and enthroned Emperor Xiaozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue remonstrated calmly; Rong soon saw his error and enthroned Emperor Xiaozhuang.

sentences.zh: 以定策功，賜爵樊城鄉男。

translations.literal: For merit in settling the policy he was ennobled as Baron of Fancheng Township.
translations.idiomatic: For helping settle the succession he was made Baron of Fancheng Township.

sentences.zh: 從榮破葛榮，平元顥，累遷左光祿大夫、武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Following Rong he defeated Ge Rong and pacified Yuan Hao, and was repeatedly promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Rong against Ge Rong and Yuan Hao and rose to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 時万俟醜奴僭稱大號，關中騷動，榮將遣嶽討之。

translations.literal: At that time Moqi Chounu usurped a great title and Guanzhong was in turmoil; Rong was about to send Yue to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Chounu had proclaimed himself emperor and Guanzhong was in uproar; Rong meant to send Yue against him.

sentences.zh: 私謂其兄勝曰：「醜奴足為勍敵，若嶽往無功，罪責立至；

translations.literal: Privately he told his elder brother Sheng, "Chounu is fully a formidable foe; if Yue goes and achieves nothing, blame will come at once;
translations.idiomatic: In private he told Sheng, "Chounu is a formidable foe—if I fail, punishment follows at once;

sentences.zh: 假令克定，恐讒訴生焉。」

translations.literal: even if we were to conquer and settle matters, I fear slander would arise."
translations.idiomatic: and even if I win, slander will surely follow."

sentences.zh: 乃請爾硃氏一人為元帥，岳副貳之。

translations.literal: He thereupon asked that one of the Erzhu clan serve as commander-in-chief and Yue be second to him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked that an Erzhu lead the army while he served as second.

sentences.zh: 榮大悅，乃以天光為使持節、大都督、雍州刺史，以岳為左廂大都督，又以征西將軍侯莫陳悅為右廂大都督，並為天光之副，以討之。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly pleased and thereupon made Tianguang Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and Regional Inspector of Yong Province; made Yue Grand Commander of the Left Wing and also made General of the Western Campaign Houmochen Yue Grand Commander of the Right Wing—all as Tianguang's deputies—to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was delighted and appointed Tianguang Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander, and Regional Inspector of Yong; Yue as commander of the left wing and Houmochen Yue of the right, both under Tianguang, to campaign against Chounu.

sentences.zh: 時赤水蜀賊兵斷路，天光眾不滿二千。

translations.literal: At that time Shu rebels of Chishui blocked the road; Tianguang's host was fewer than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu bandits of Chishui blocked the roads; Tianguang had fewer than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 及軍次潼關，天光有難色，嶽乃進破之於渭北，軍容大振。

translations.literal: When the army reached Tong Pass, Tianguang showed a troubled countenance; Yue advanced and defeated them north of the Wei, and the army's bearing was greatly uplifted.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass Tianguang looked uneasy; Yue advanced, routed the enemy north of the Wei, and the army's spirit soared.

sentences.zh: 時醜奴自圍岐州，遣其大行台尉遲菩薩、僕射万俟行醜同向武功，南度渭水，攻圍趨柵。

translations.literal: At that time Chounu himself was besieging Qi Province and sent his Grand Branch Censor Yuchi Pusa and Vice Director Moqi Xingchou together toward Wugong; they crossed the Wei River southward and attacked and besieged the stockade at Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu was besieging Qi Province and sent his Grand Branch Censor Yuchi Pusa and Vice Director Moqi Xingchou toward Wugong; crossing the Wei south, they assaulted the stockade at Qu.

sentences.zh: 天光遣嶽率千騎赴援。

translations.literal: Tianguang sent Yue with a thousand horsemen to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang sent Yue with a thousand horsemen to relieve the post.

sentences.zh: 菩薩攻柵已克，率步騎二萬至渭北。

translations.literal: Pusa had already taken the stockade and led twenty thousand foot and horse to the north bank of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pusa had already taken the stockade and brought twenty thousand foot and horse to the north bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 嶽以輕騎數十，與菩薩隔水交言。

translations.literal: Yue with several tens of light horsemen exchanged words with Pusa across the water.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took a few dozen light horsemen and parleyed with Pusa across the river.

sentences.zh: 岳稱揚國威，菩薩乃自驕，令省事傳語。

translations.literal: Yue proclaimed the state's majesty; Pusa thereupon grew arrogant himself and ordered a clerk to convey his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yue proclaimed the empire's might; Pusa grew haughty and sent a clerk to answer.

sentences.zh: 省事恃水，應答不遜。

translations.literal: The clerk, relying on the water, answered without deference.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk, safe across the water, replied insolently.

sentences.zh: 嶽怒，舉弓射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Yue was angry, raised his bow and shot him; at the twang of the string he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yue in anger shot him down at the twang of the bow.

sentences.zh: 時已逼暮，於是各還。

translations.literal: It was already near dusk, and they thereupon each withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk was near; both sides withdrew.

sentences.zh: 岳于渭南傍水，分精兵數十為一處，隨地形勢置之。

translations.literal: Yue, by the Wei south of Weinan, divided elite troops in groups of several tens to a place and set them according to the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: South of Weinan along the Wei, Yue hid picked men in dozens of small groups, placed to suit the ground.

sentences.zh: 明日，將百餘騎，隔水與賊相見，且並東行。

translations.literal: The next day he led a little more than a hundred horsemen, showed himself to the enemy across the water, and together moved east.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he led a little over a hundred horsemen, showed himself across the river, and drifted east with the enemy in view.

sentences.zh: 嶽漸前進，先所置騎，隨嶽而集，騎既漸增，賊不復測其多少。

translations.literal: Yue gradually advanced; the horsemen he had placed earlier gathered with Yue as he went, and as the horsemen steadily increased the enemy could no longer gauge their number.
translations.idiomatic: As Yue edged forward, his hidden riders joined him one by one; the column swelled until the enemy could no longer tell how many he had.

sentences.zh: 行二十許裏，至水淺可濟處，岳便馳馬東出，似欲奔遁。

translations.literal: After traveling some twenty li they reached a shallow ford; Yue thereupon galloped east as though intending to flee.
translations.idiomatic: After some twenty li they came to a shallow ford; Yue suddenly spurred east as if to flee.

sentences.zh: 賊謂嶽走，乃棄步兵，南度渭水，輕騎追嶽。

translations.literal: The enemy thought Yue was running away, thereupon abandoned the foot soldiers, crossed the Wei southward, and with light cavalry pursued Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought him routed, dropped their infantry, crossed the Wei, and chased with light horse.

sentences.zh: 岳東行十餘里，依橫岡設伏兵以待之，身先士卒，急擊之，賊便退走。

translations.literal: Yue went east more than ten li, laid ambush along a transverse ridge to await them, took the lead before the soldiers himself, struck them urgently, and the enemy at once retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li farther east he ambushed them along a ridge, led the charge himself, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 嶽號令所部，賊下馬者皆不聽殺。

translations.literal: Yue ordered his troops that any enemy who dismounted was not to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue ordered his men not to kill any rebel who dismounted.

sentences.zh: 賊顧見之，便悉投馬。

translations.literal: The enemy, looking back and seeing this, thereupon all cast themselves from their horses.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this, the rebels all leapt from their horses.

sentences.zh: 俄虜三千人。

translations.literal: In no time they captured three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In moments they took three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 馬亦無遺，遂禽菩薩。

translations.literal: Not a horse was left either, and they thereupon captured Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: Not a horse was left; they captured Pusa.

sentences.zh: 仍度渭北，降步卒萬餘。

translations.literal: They then crossed to the north bank of the Wei and received the surrender of more than ten thousand foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed back north of the Wei and accepted the surrender of more than ten thousand foot.

sentences.zh: 醜奴尋棄岐州，北走安定。

translations.literal: Chounu soon abandoned Qi Province and fled north to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu soon abandoned Qi Province and fled north to Anding.

sentences.zh: 天光方自雍至，與嶽合勢。

translations.literal: Tianguang had just arrived from Yong, and united his strength with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang had just come up from Yong and joined forces with Yue.

sentences.zh: 宣言今氣候已熱，非征討之時，待至秋涼，更圖進取。

translations.literal: They proclaimed that the season was already hot and not a time for campaigning, and that they would wait until autumn grew cool before plotting further advance.
translations.idiomatic: They announced that the heat had come and the season was no time for war; they would wait for autumn's cool and then plan their next move.

sentences.zh: 醜奴聞之，遂以為實，分遣諸軍散營農於岐州北百里網川。

translations.literal: When Chounu heard this, he took it for truth, and dispersed his armies to camp and farm in Wangchuan, a hundred li north of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu believed them, sent his armies to scatter and farm in Wangchuan, a hundred li north of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 使太尉侯伏侯元進據險立柵。

translations.literal: He had Grand Marshal Houfu Hou Yuanjin seize the heights and build a stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Grand Marshal Houfu Hou Yuanjin on the heights behind palisades.

sentences.zh: 嶽知其勢分，密與天光嚴備。

translations.literal: Yue knew their force was divided, and secretly made strict preparations with Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue saw their strength was split and quietly made ready with Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 昧旦，攻圍元進柵，拔之，即禽元進，自余諸柵悉降。

translations.literal: At daybreak they attacked and besieged Yuanjin's stockade, took it, and at once captured Yuanjin; all the other stockades surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they stormed Yuanjin's camp, seized it, and took Yuanjin himself; every other palisade submitted.

sentences.zh: 又輕騎追醜奴，及之於平涼之長坑，一戰禽之。

translations.literal: They again pursued Chounu with light cavalry, caught him at Changkeng in Pingliang, and captured him in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Light horse then ran Chounu down to Changkeng in Pingliang and took him in one fight.

sentences.zh: 高平城中又執蕭寶夤以歸。

translations.literal: Within Gaoping city they also seized Xiao Baoyin and brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping too seized Xiao Baoyin and delivered him up.

sentences.zh: 賊行台万俟道洛退保牽屯，嶽攻之。

translations.literal: The rebel Commissioner Moqi Daoluo withdrew to defend Qiantun; Yue attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commissioner Moqi Daoluo fell back on Qiantun; Yue assailed him.

sentences.zh: 道洛敗入隴，投略陽賊帥王慶雲。

translations.literal: Daoluo was defeated and entered Long, throwing himself on the Lueyang bandit chief Wang Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Daoluo, beaten, crossed into Long and sought refuge with the Lueyang rebel Wang Qingyun.

sentences.zh: 以道洛驍果絕倫，得之甚喜，以為將。

translations.literal: Because Daoluo's valor and daring were unmatched, Qingyun was greatly pleased to gain him and made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun was delighted to have so peerless a fighter and made him his general.

sentences.zh: 天光又與嶽度隴，至慶雲所居永洛城。

translations.literal: Tianguang again crossed Long with Yue and reached Yongluo, where Qingyun dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang and Yue crossed Long again and came to Yongluo, Qingyun's seat.

sentences.zh: 慶雲、道洛頻出城拒戰，並禽之，餘眾皆悉坑之。

translations.literal: Qingyun and Daoluo repeatedly came out to fight and were both captured; the rest of the host were all buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyun and Daoluo sallied again and again and were both taken; the remainder were put to the sword and buried in the pits.

sentences.zh: 三秦、河、渭、瓜、涼、鄯州咸來歸款。

translations.literal: The three Qins and the provinces of He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shan all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Qins and the provinces of He, Wei, Gua, Liang, and Shan all tendered allegiance.

sentences.zh: 賊帥夏州人宿勤明達降復叛，嶽又討禽之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Suqin Mingda of Xiazhou submitted and rebelled again; Yue campaigned once more and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiazhou rebel Suqin Mingda surrendered, then rose again; Yue marched out and took him.

sentences.zh: 天光雖為元帥，而岳功效居多，進封樊城縣伯。

translations.literal: Although Tianguang was commander-in-chief, Yue's achievements were the greater part, and he was advanced to Marquis of Fancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang held the supreme command, yet most of the credit was Yue's; Yue was raised to Marquis of Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋詔岳都督、涇州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon an edict made Yue Area Commander and Inspector of Jingzhou, advancing his rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon named him Area Commander and Inspector of Jing, with the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 天光入洛，使嶽行雍州事。

translations.literal: When Tianguang entered Luoyang, he had Yue act for the affairs of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang went to Luoyang, Yue was left to govern Yong.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除都督、岐州刺史，進清水郡公，尋加侍中，給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was appointed Area Commander and Inspector of Qizhou, advanced to Duke of Qingshui commandery, and soon made Attendant-in-Ordinary with rear guard music granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai he became Area Commander and Inspector of Qi, was made Duke of Qingshui, and soon received the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary with an imperial band.

sentences.zh: 進位開府儀同三司兼尚書左僕射、隴右行台，仍停高平。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Commissioner of the Longyou Circuit, and still remained at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies, with concurrent posts as Left Vice Director and Commissioner for Longyou, and still kept his base at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 後以隴中猶有土人不順，岳助侯莫陳悅，所在討平之。

translations.literal: Later, because there were still native chiefs in Long who would not submit, Yue aided Houmochen Yue in pacifying them wherever they were found.
translations.idiomatic: When native leaders in Long still held out, Yue aided Houmochen Yue in hunting them down wherever they appeared.

sentences.zh: 二年，加都督、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was additionally made Area Commander and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he was also named Area Commander and Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 天光將拒齊神武，遣問計于嶽。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was about to oppose Gao Huan, he sent to ask Yue's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: As Tianguang prepared to face Gao Huan, he asked Yue's advice.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「莫若且鎮關中，以固根本。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "Better to hold Guanzhong for now and secure the root."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Hold Guanzhong first and shore up your base."

sentences.zh: 天光不從，後果敗。

translations.literal: Tianguang did not follow this, and in the end was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang would not heed him and was ruined.

sentences.zh: 嶽率軍下隴赴雍，禽天光弟顯壽以應齊神武。

translations.literal: Yue led his army down from Long to Yong, captured Tianguang's younger brother Xianshou, and responded to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Yue marched down from Long to Yong, seized Tianguang's brother Xianshou, and threw in with Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 及孝武即位，加關中大行台。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Yue was additionally made Grand Commissioner of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended, Yue was made Grand Commissioner of Guanzhong as well.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，孝武密令岳圖齊神武，遂刺心血，持以寄嶽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Xiaowu secretly ordered Yue to plot against Gao Huan, and pricked his heart's blood to send to Yue.
