translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year two the emperor secretly charged Yue to move against Gao Huan and pricked his own heart's blood to send as pledge.

sentences.zh: 嶽懼，乃自詣北境，安置邊防，率眾趨平涼西界，布營數十里，托以牧馬于原州，為自安之計。

translations.literal: Yue was afraid, and so went in person to the northern frontier, set the border defenses in order, led his host to the western marches of Pingliang, pitched camps for several tens of li, and under the pretext of pasturing horses at Yuanzhou made plans for his own security.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Yue went north himself, set the frontier in order, and led his men to Pingliang's western border, where he strung camps along dozens of li, claiming to graze horses at Yuanzhou while he looked to his own safety.

sentences.zh: 先是，費也頭万俟受洛幹、鐵勒斛律沙門、解拔彌俄突、紇豆陵伊利等擁眾自守，至是皆款附。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Feituo chief Moqi Shouluogan, the Tiele chief Hulu Shamen, the Xianbei chief Mie'etuo, the Gedouling chief Yili, and others had held their followers and kept themselves apart; now they all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Before this Moqi Shouluogan of the Feituo, Hulu Shamen of the Tiele, Mie'etuo of the Xianbei, Yili of the Gedouling, and other chiefs who had held their peoples apart now all tendered allegiance.

sentences.zh: 秦、南秦、河、渭四州刺史又會平涼，受嶽節度。

translations.literal: The inspectors of Qin, Southern Qin, He, and Wei again assembled at Pingliang and accepted Yue's command.
translations.idiomatic: The inspectors of Qin, Southern Qin, He, and Wei met again at Pingliang and placed themselves under Yue.

sentences.zh: 唯靈州刺史曹泥不應召，通使于齊神武。

translations.literal: Only Cao Ni, Inspector of Lingzhou, did not answer the summons and sent envoys to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Only Cao Ni of Lingzhou ignored the call and opened correspondence with Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武乃遣左丞翟嵩使至關中，間岳及侯莫陣悅。

translations.literal: Gao Huan then sent the Left Assistant Director Zhai Song as envoy to Guanzhong to sound out Yue and Houmochen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent his Left Assistant Director Zhai Song to Guanzhong to probe Yue and Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 三年，嶽召悅會于高平，將討曹泥，令悅前驅，而悅受神武指，密圖嶽。

translations.literal: In the third year Heba Yue summoned Houmochen Yue to meet at Gaoping, intending to campaign against Cao Ni and ordering Yue as vanguard; but Yue had received Gao Huan's instructions and secretly plotted against Heba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Heba Yue called Houmochen Yue to Gaoping to strike Cao Ni and set him in the van; yet Houmochen Yue had taken Gao Huan's cue and was secretly plotting Heba Yue's death.

sentences.zh: 嶽弗之知，而先又輕悅，悅乃誘岳入營，共論兵事。

translations.literal: Heba Yue did not know this, and moreover had earlier looked down on Houmochen Yue; Houmochen Yue then lured Heba Yue into camp to discuss military affairs together.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue knew nothing of it and had long held Houmochen Yue cheap; Houmochen Yue lured him into camp on the pretext of discussing strategy.

sentences.zh: 悅詐云腹痛，起而徐行，令其婿元洪景斬岳於幕中。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue pretended a pain in the belly, rose and walked slowly, and had his son-in-law Yuan Hongjing cut Heba Yue down inside the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue feigned a bellyache, rose and strolled away, and had his son-in-law Yuan Hongjing strike Heba Yue down in the tent.

sentences.zh: 朝野莫不痛惜之。

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country mourned him alike.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、太傅、錄尚書事、都督關中二十州諸軍事、大將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰武莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Area Commander over the military affairs of twenty Guanzhong provinces, Grand General, and Inspector of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Martial and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Tutor, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with command over twenty Guanzhong provinces as Grand General and Inspector of Yong, posthumous name Martial and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 翟嵩復命于神武，神武下床鳴其頰曰：「除吾病者，卿也，何日忘之！」

translations.literal: Zhai Song reported back to Gao Huan; Gao Huan came down from the couch and slapped his own cheek, saying: "You are the one who cured my illness—how could I ever forget!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Song returned to Gao Huan, who stepped from his couch and struck his own cheek, crying, "You cured my sickness—when shall I forget you!"

sentences.zh: 後岳部下收岳屍，葬於雍州北石安原，葬以王禮。

translations.literal: Later Yue's followers recovered Yue's corpse and buried it at Shianyuan north of Yongzhou, with the rites due a king.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yue's men recovered his body and buried him at Shianyuan north of Yong with royal honors.

sentences.zh: 子緯嗣，拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Wei succeeded him and was appointed Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei succeeded him and received the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 周保定中，錄嶽舊德，進爵霍國公，尚周文帝女。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era of Zhou, recording Yue's former merit, Wei was advanced to Duke of the State of Huo and married a daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Baoding his father's merit was remembered: he was made Duke of Huo and wed a daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅，代人也。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父婆羅門為駝牛都尉，故悅長於河西。

translations.literal: His father Boluomen was Commandant of Camel Cattle, and so Yue grew up in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Boluomen had been Commandant of the Camel Herds, and Yue was raised in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 好田獵，便騎射，會牧子作亂，遂歸爾硃榮。

translations.literal: He loved hunting and was skilled at mounted archery; when the pastoral tribes rose in rebellion, he went over to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the chase and rode and shot with ease; when the pastoral peoples rebelled he entered Erzhu Rong's service.

sentences.zh: 榮引為府長流參軍。

translations.literal: Rong brought him in as Senior Adjutant of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Rong made him Senior Adjutant on his staff.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，除金紫光祿大夫，封柏人縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Marquis of Boren county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang came to the throne he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis of Boren.

sentences.zh: 爾硃天光之討關西，榮以悅為天光右廂大都督。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang campaigned in Guanxi, Rong made Yue Grand Commander of Tianguang's right wing.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tianguang marched on Guanxi, Rong named Yue Grand Commander of his right wing.

sentences.zh: 西伐克獲，皆與天光、賀拔嶽略同。

translations.literal: In the western campaigns his captures and victories were much the same as Tianguang's and Heba Yue's.
translations.idiomatic: In the western wars his victories matched those of Tianguang and Heba Yue.

sentences.zh: 除鄯州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Inspector of Shan.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死後，亦隨天光下隴。

translations.literal: After Erzhu Rong's death he also followed Tianguang down from Long.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death he followed Tianguang down from Long.

sentences.zh: 元曄立，進爵為公，改封白水郡公。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was established, Yue's rank was advanced to duke and his fief changed to Duke of Baishui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned he was raised to duke and enfeoffed as Duke of Baishui.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，除秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In Putai he was appointed Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Putai he became Inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 天光之東出，將抗齊神武，悅與嶽下隴以應神武，至雍州，會爾硃覆敗。

translations.literal: When Tianguang marched east to oppose Gao Huan, Houmochen Yue and Heba Yue came down from Long to answer Gao Huan; they reached Yongzhou just as the Erzhu clan met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang went east to face Gao Huan, Houmochen Yue and Heba Yue descended from Long to join Gao Huan and reached Yong as the Erzhu house collapsed.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，加開府儀同三司、都督隴右諸軍事，仍兼秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was additionally given the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies and made Area Commander over the military affairs of Longyou, still concurrently Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxi he received the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies and command over Longyou while retaining Qin.

sentences.zh: 三年，嶽召悅共討曹泥，悅誘嶽斬之。

translations.literal: In the third year Heba Yue summoned Houmochen Yue to campaign jointly against Cao Ni, and Houmochen Yue lured Heba Yue in and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Heba Yue called him to join the strike on Cao Ni; Houmochen Yue lured him in and killed him.

sentences.zh: 嶽左右奔散，悅遣人安慰，眾皆畏服。

translations.literal: Yue's attendants scattered in flight; Yue sent men to reassure them, and the host all submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's men broke and fled; Yue sent word to calm them, and the army bowed in fear.

sentences.zh: 悅心猶豫，不即撫納，乃還入隴，止永洛城。

translations.literal: Yue's heart hesitated; he did not at once win them over, but returned into Long and halted at Yongluo.
translations.idiomatic: His heart wavered; he did not rally them at once but withdrew into Long and held Yongluo.

sentences.zh: 岳所部聚於平涼，規還圖悅。

translations.literal: Yue's former command gathered at Pingliang and plotted to turn back against Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's old command massed at Pingliang and planned to turn on Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 周文帝時為夏州刺史，眾遣奉迎。

translations.literal: At that time the future Emperor Wen of Zhou was Inspector of Xiazhou, and the host sent to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Wen of Zhou was then Inspector of Xia, and the troops sent to bring him in.

sentences.zh: 周文至，遂總嶽部眾並家口入高平城，以自安固。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen arrived, he then gathered Yue's troops and their families into Gaoping city to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wen came he took over Yue's soldiers and families and shut them within Gaoping to make himself safe.

sentences.zh: 乃勒眾入隴征悅。

translations.literal: He then drove the host into Long to campaign against Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the army into Long against Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 悅聞之，棄城南據山水之險。

translations.literal: When Houmochen Yue heard of it, he abandoned the city and held the peril of mountains and waters to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Houmochen Yue abandoned the city and clung to the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 悅先召南秦州刺史李景和。

translations.literal: Yue had earlier summoned Li Jinghe, Inspector of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had already called up Li Jinghe, Inspector of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 其夜景和遣人詣周文，密許翻降。

translations.literal: That night Jinghe sent a man to Zhou Wen and secretly promised to turn and submit.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jinghe sent a man to Zhou Wen and secretly pledged to defect.

sentences.zh: 至暮，景和乃勒其所部，使上驢駝，云：「儀同有教，欲還秦州，守以拒賊。」

translations.literal: At dusk Jinghe then mustered his command, had them mount donkeys and camels, and said: "The Bearer of the Staff has orders: we are to return to Qinzhou and hold it against the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Jinghe mustered his men, had them mount asses and camels, and announced, "Our commander orders us back to Qin to hold the province against the enemy."

sentences.zh: 復給帳下云：「儀同欲還秦州，汝等何不裝辦？」

translations.literal: He again told those under his tent: "The Bearer of the Staff wishes to return to Qinzhou—why do you not pack?"
translations.idiomatic: He told his tent guard, "The commander is returning to Qin—why haven't you packed?"

sentences.zh: 眾謂言實，以次相驚，皆散趣秦州。

translations.literal: The host took the words for truth; one after another they were alarmed and all scattered toward Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The men believed him; panic ran down the ranks and they broke for Qin.

sentences.zh: 景和先馳至城，據門以慰輯之。

translations.literal: Jinghe galloped ahead to the city, seized the gate, and calmed and gathered them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe raced ahead, seized the gate, and calmed the fugitives as they arrived.

sentences.zh: 悅部眾離散，猜畏傍人，不聽左右近己。

translations.literal: Yue's troops scattered; suspicious and afraid of those beside him, he would not let attendants come near.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's force melted away; paranoid and afraid, he would let no one approach.

sentences.zh: 與其二弟井兒及謀殺嶽者八九人，棄軍迸走，數日之中，盤回往來，不知所趣。

translations.literal: With his two younger brothers Jing'er and the eight or nine men who had plotted Yue's murder, he abandoned the army and fled headlong; for several days they wandered back and forth, not knowing where to go.
translations.idiomatic: With his brothers Jing'er and the eight or nine who had killed Yue he abandoned the army and fled; for days they circled the hills without knowing where to turn.

sentences.zh: 左右勸向靈州，而悅不決。

translations.literal: Those beside him urged him toward Lingzhou, but Yue could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: His companions urged Lingzhou, but he could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 言下隴後恐為人見，乃放馬山中，令從者悉步，自乘一騾，欲往靈州。

translations.literal: Saying that after descending Long he feared being seen, he turned the horses loose in the mountains, made his followers all go on foot, and himself rode a single mule, intending to go to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing eyes on the road down from Long, he turned his horses loose in the hills, made his men walk, and rode a mule alone toward Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 中路追騎將及，縊死野中。

translations.literal: Midway pursuing horsemen were about to overtake him; he hanged himself in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers were closing in; he hanged himself in the open country.

sentences.zh: 弟息部下，悉見禽殺。

translations.literal: His younger brothers, sons, and followers were all captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers, sons, and men were all taken and slain.

sentences.zh: 唯先謀殺嶽者悅中兵參軍豆盧光，走至靈州，後奔晉陽。

translations.literal: Only Dou Lu Guang, the Staff Adjutant in Yue's central army who had first plotted Yue's murder, fled to Lingzhou and later ran to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dou Lu Guang, the staff adjutant who had struck the first blow against Yue, escaped to Ling and later fled to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 悅自殺嶽後，精神恍惚，不復如常。

translations.literal: After Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, his spirit was dazed and no longer as before.
translations.idiomatic: After he killed Heba Yue his mind never settled; he was not himself again.

sentences.zh: 恆言：「我睡即夢嶽語我'兄欲何處去？

translations.literal: He constantly said: "When I sleep I dream that Heba Yue speaks to me: 'Elder brother, where do you mean to go?
translations.idiomatic: He kept saying, "When I sleep Heba Yue comes to me in dreams: 'Brother, where are you going?

sentences.zh: '隨逐我不相置。」

translations.literal: He pursues me and will not leave me."
translations.idiomatic: He dogs my steps and will not let me be."

sentences.zh: 因此彌不自安，而致敗滅。

translations.literal: Because of this he was all the more ill at ease, and so met defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The more he brooded, the less peace he had, until ruin took him.

sentences.zh: 念賢，字蓋盧，金城枹罕人也。

translations.literal: Nianxian, style name Gailu, was a native of Fuhan in Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Nianxian, styled Gailu, came from Fuhan in Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 父求就，以大家子戍武川鎮，仍家焉。

translations.literal: His father Qiujiu, as the son of a great house, garrisoned Wuchuan fortress and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiujiu, born to a great clan, was posted to Wuchuan and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 賢美容質，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: Nianxian was handsome in bearing and had dipped into the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Nianxian was fair of face and had read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 為兒童時，在學中讀書，有善相者過學，諸生競詣之。

translations.literal: As a child, while reading in school, a skilled physiognomist passed the academy and the students all rushed to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy in school a fortune-teller passed by; the pupils all crowded to have their fortunes read.

sentences.zh: 賢獨不往，笑謂諸生曰：「男兒死生富貴，皆在天也，何遽相乎！」

translations.literal: Nianxian alone did not go, and laughing said to the students: "A man's death, life, wealth, and honor are all in Heaven—why hurry to have your fates told!"
translations.idiomatic: Nianxian alone stayed back and laughed at them: "Life, death, wealth, and rank are Heaven's to give—why rush to a stranger's guess!"

sentences.zh: 少遭父憂，居喪有孝稱。

translations.literal: In youth he suffered his father's death and in mourning won a name for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father young and was praised for the mourning he kept.

sentences.zh: 後以破衛可環功，除別將，又以軍功封屯留縣伯。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in defeating the Rouran chief Kehuan, he was made Separate Commander, and again for military achievement was enfeoffed as Earl of Tunliu county.
translations.idiomatic: For breaking the Rouran chief Kehuan he was made Separate Commander; further victories won him the earldom of Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 從爾硃榮入洛，兼尚書右僕射、東道行台，進爵平恩縣公。

translations.literal: Following Erzhu Rong into Luoyang, he was concurrently Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Commissioner of the Eastern Circuit, and advanced to Duke of Ping'en county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Rong to Luoyang as Right Vice Director and Commissioner of the Eastern Circuit and was made Duke of Ping'en.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，孝武以賢為中軍北向大都督，進爵安定郡公，加侍中、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In Yongxi, Emperor Xiaowu made Nianxian Grand Commander of the Center Army facing north, advanced him to Duke of Anding commandery, and added Attendant-in-Ordinary and Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongxi Emperor Xiaowu named him Grand Commander of the Center Army facing north, Duke of Anding, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 大統初，拜太尉，為秦州刺史，加太傅，給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was appointed Grand Commandant, made Inspector of Qinzhou, given the Grand Tutorship, and granted rear guard music.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong he became Grand Commandant and Inspector of Qin, with the Grand Tutorship and an imperial band.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉太師、都督、河州刺史、大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Grand Preceptor, Area Commander, Inspector of Hezhou, and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he became Grand Preceptor, Area Commander, Inspector of He, and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 久之還朝，兼錄尚書事。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to court and was made concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in the provinces he returned to court as Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後與廣陵王欣、扶風王季等同為正直侍中。

translations.literal: Later he was made Upright Attendant-in-Ordinary together with the Prince of Guangling, Xin, the Prince of Fufeng, Ji, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Upright Attendant-in-Ordinary alongside Princes Xin of Guangling and Ji of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 時行殿初成，未有題目，帝詔近侍各名之，對者非一，莫允帝心。

translations.literal: At that time the traveling hall was newly completed and had no name; the emperor ordered those close at hand each to name it. Many answers were given, but none pleased the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: When the traveling hall was newly built it bore no name; the emperor asked his intimates each to propose one. Many titles were offered, none to his liking.

sentences.zh: 賢乃為「圓極」，帝笑曰：「正與朕意同。」

translations.literal: Nianxian then offered "Round Ultimate"; the emperor smiled and said: "That is exactly of one mind with me."
translations.idiomatic: Nianxian proposed "Round Ultimate"; the emperor smiled and said, "That is precisely my thought.

sentences.zh: 即名之。

translations.literal: He at once gave it that name.
translations.idiomatic: He at once gave the hall that name.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，賢不力戰，乃先還，自是名頗減。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao, Nianxian did not fight with full force and returned first; from then his reputation declined somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao he did not press the fight and withdrew early; his standing never quite recovered.

sentences.zh: 五年，除都督、秦州刺史，薨于州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Area Commander and Inspector of Qinzhou, and died in office in that province.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was made Area Commander and Inspector of Qin and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 諡曰昭定。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Bright and Settled.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Bright and Settled.

sentences.zh: 賢于諸公，皆為父党，自周文以下，咸拜敬之。

translations.literal: Among the nobles Nianxian stood as father-generation kin to them all; from Zhou Wen downward they all bowed to him in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Among the great lords he counted as their fathers' generation; from Zhou Wen down all showed him the bow due an elder.

sentences.zh: 子華，性和厚，有長者風。

translations.literal: His son Zihua was by nature gentle and generous and had the bearing of an elder.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zihua was gentle and steadfast, with the dignified air of a man of years.

sentences.zh: 官至開府儀同三司、合州刺史。

translations.literal: His offices reached Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the three highest ministers and Regional Inspector of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master of the Palace, rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and served as Regional Inspector of He Province.

sentences.zh: 梁覽，字景睿，金城人也。

translations.literal: Liang Lan, style name Jingrui, was a native of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Lan, whose style was Jingrui, came from Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 其先出自安定，避難走西羌，世為部落酋帥。

translations.literal: His forebears came forth from Anding; fleeing trouble they went among the Western Qiang and for generations were chieftains of tribal confederations.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were from Anding; fleeing turmoil they took refuge among the Western Qiang, where for generations they led their tribes as chieftains.

sentences.zh: 曾祖穆，以枹罕城歸吐谷渾，後又歸魏，封臨洮公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Mu, having surrendered Baohen city to Tuyuhun, later returned to Wei and was enfeoffed as Duke of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Mu yielded Baohen to Tuyuhun, then came over to Wei and was made Duke of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 祖顥，為尚書，封南安公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hao served as Minister of the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hao held the post of Minister of the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed Duke of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 父釗，河華二州刺史，封新陽縣伯。

translations.literal: His father Zhao was Regional Inspector of the two provinces He and Hua and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinyang County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao was Regional Inspector of He and Hua and held the county marquisate of Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 覽家世豪富，貲累千金。

translations.literal: Lan's family for generations was grandly wealthy, with wealth accumulated to a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: The Lan family had been wealthy for generations, their riches reckoned in thousands of gold.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，秦州莫折念生、胡琛等反，散財招募，有二千人，鎮河州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Moqi Niansheng of Qin Province, Hu Chen, and others rebelled; he dispersed his wealth to recruit men, had two thousand men, and garrisoned He Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era, when Moqi Niansheng of Qin and Hu Chen and others rose in revolt, Lan spent his fortune to raise troops—two thousand men—and held He Province.

sentences.zh: 從大軍平賊，曆涼、河二州刺史，封安德縣侯。

translations.literal: Following the great army in pacifying the rebels, he served in turn as Regional Inspector of Liang and He and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ande County.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with the main forces to crush the rebels, served successively as Regional Inspector of Liang and He, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Ande.

sentences.zh: 覽既為本州刺史，盛修甲仗，人馬精銳。

translations.literal: Once Lan became Regional Inspector of his native province, he greatly repaired armor and weapons; men and horses were keen and elite.
translations.idiomatic: As native governor, he heavily outfitted arms and armor; his men and horses were trained and sharp.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾憚不敢出，皆曰：「梁公在，未可行也。」

translations.literal: Tuyuhun feared him and did not dare come forth; all said, "While Lord Liang is here, one may not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun dared not stir; everyone said, "With Lord Liang on the frontier, nothing can be done.

sentences.zh: 永安中，詔大鴻臚琅邪王皓就策授世為河州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yongan, an edict had the Grand Master of Ceremonies, Wang Hao of Langya, go to confer by document the hereditary post of Regional Inspector of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan, the emperor ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies Wang Hao of Langye to go and invest his line with the hereditary governorship of He Province.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，改封郡公。

translations.literal: In Yongxi, his enfeoffment was changed to that of a dukedom.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was raised to a duke.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，加太尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, he was given the additional office of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 其年，覽從弟ＧＣ定反，欲圖覽，覽與數戰未能平，王師至，始破之。

translations.literal: That year Lan's younger cousin Liang Xingding rebelled and plotted against Lan; Lan fought him several times but could not pacify him, and only when the imperial army arrived was he at last broken.
translations.idiomatic: That same year his cousin Liang Xingding rebelled and plotted his death; Lan fought him repeatedly without success until the central army arrived and broke the revolt.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷太傅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 及河橋之役，王師敗，時病留長安，趙青雀反北城，覽為之謀主。

translations.literal: At the time of the battle at Heqiao, the imperial army was defeated; he was then ill and remained in Chang'an; Zhao Qingque rebelled in the north city, and Lan was the chief planner for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heqiao campaign ended in defeat, Lan, sick and left in Chang'an, became chief strategist to Zhao Qingque, who rose in the north city.

sentences.zh: 事平，乃見殺。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified, he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the rising was put down, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 子鸛雀，位儀同三司、大都督，後坐事免，死。

translations.literal: His son Guanque held the posts of Pusang and Grand Commander-in-Chief; later he was dismissed on account of an offense and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guanque held the ranks of Pusang and Grand Commander; later he was dismissed for an offense and died.

sentences.zh: 雷紹，字道宗，武川鎮人也。

translations.literal: Lei Shao, style name Daozong, was a native of Wuchuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Shao, style Daozong, was from Wuchuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 九歲而孤。

translations.literal: At nine he lost his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned at nine.

sentences.zh: 有膂力，善騎射。

translations.literal: He had strength in his muscles and was skilled at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: He was powerfully built and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 年十八，給事鎮府。

translations.literal: At eighteen he served in attendance at the garrison headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he entered service at the garrison seat.

sentences.zh: 嘗使洛陽。

translations.literal: He was once sent on mission to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 見京都禮義之美，還謂同僚曰：「徒知邊備尚武，以圖富貴；

translations.literal: Seeing the beauty of ritual and propriety in the capital, on his return he told his colleagues, "We only know that on the frontier we esteem martial valor to pursue wealth and rank;
translations.idiomatic: Struck by the refinement of the capital, he told his comrades on returning, "We frontier folk think only of arms and valor to win fortune;

sentences.zh: 不謂文學，身之寶也。

translations.literal: we do not consider that literary learning is the treasure of the person.
translations.idiomatic: we never reckon that learning is a man's true wealth.

sentences.zh: 生世不學，其猶穴處，何所見焉？」

translations.literal: To live in the world without learning is like dwelling in a cave—what would one ever see?
translations.idiomatic: To live unlettered in this world is to live in a burrow—what can you ever see?

sentences.zh: 遂逃歸，辭母求師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fled home, took leave of his mother, and sought a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He fled home, bade farewell to his mother, and went in search of instruction.

sentences.zh: 經年，通《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: Within a year he had mastered the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and the 《Analects》.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he had mastered the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and the 《Analects》.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀書至人行莫大於孝，乃投卷歎曰：「吾離違侍養，非人子之道。」

translations.literal: Once reading to the passage that among human conduct nothing is greater than filial piety, he cast down his scroll and sighed, "I have left and violated attending and nourishing—this is not the way of a son.
translations.idiomatic: Reading once that nothing in human conduct surpasses filial piety, he flung down his book and cried, "I have abandoned my mother—what son acts so?

sentences.zh: 即還鄉里，躬耕奉養。

translations.literal: Immediately he returned to his home district, personally tilling the fields to support and nourish her.
translations.idiomatic: At once he went home to farm and support her himself.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀骨立，由是知名。

translations.literal: On encountering his mother's mourning, his grief wrecked him to skin and bone; from this he became known by name.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he mourned until he was skin and bone, and his fame began from that.

sentences.zh: 鎮將召補鎮佐。

translations.literal: The garrison commander summoned him to fill a supplementary post as garrison assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander called him to serve as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 後隨賀拔嶽征討，為岳長史。

translations.literal: Later he followed He Bayue in campaigns and punitive expeditions, serving as Yue's Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed He Bayue on campaign and became Yue's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 岳有大事，常訪而後行。

translations.literal: When Yue had great affairs, he would consult Shao before acting.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty matters Yue always sought his counsel before acting.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武起兵，岳恥居其下。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu raised his army, Yue was shamed to stand beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shenwu took up arms, Yue could not bear to rank below him.

sentences.zh: 紹乃勸岳迎孝武西都長安，以順討逆。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon urged Yue to welcome Emperor Xiaowu west to establish his capital at Chang'an, using compliance to punish rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shao urged Yue to welcome Emperor Xiaowu west to Chang'an and strike down the rebel from a righteous position.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「吾本意也。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "That is my original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "That has been my intent all along.

sentences.zh: 後岳信諸將言，欲保關中，坐觀成敗。

translations.literal: Later Yue believed the generals' words and wished to hold Guanzhong, sitting and watching success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yue listened to his generals and chose to hold Guanzhong, sitting out the contest.

sentences.zh: 紹知計不用，請為邊州，建功效。

translations.literal: Shao knew the plan was not adopted and requested a border province where he might build merit through achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his counsel was ignored, Shao asked for a border post where he could earn merit.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「君有毗佐之力，當總大州。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "Sir, you have the strength to assist at one's side—you should oversee a great province.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "You have the makings of a chief adviser; you should govern a great province.

sentences.zh: 遂以紹為京兆太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Shao Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon made Shao Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 清平理物，甚得人和。

translations.literal: He governed with clarity and fairness and managed affairs; he greatly gained human accord.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with clarity and won the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 在郡逾年，嶽被害。

translations.literal: After more than a year in the commandery, Yue was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in office, Yue was murdered.

sentences.zh: 初，紹見岳數與侯莫陳悅宴語，嘗謂嶽曰：「公其慎之！」

translations.literal: Earlier Shao had seen Yue repeatedly feast and converse with Houmo Chenyue, and once told Yue, "My lord, be cautious of this!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shao had seen Yue feast repeatedly with Houmo Chenyue and warned him, "My lord, take care!

sentences.zh: 嶽不從，果及於難。

translations.literal: Yue did not heed him and indeed met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yue would not listen—and came to disaster.

sentences.zh: 紹乃棄郡，馳赴嶽軍，與寇洛等迎周文帝。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon abandoned his commandery and galloped to Yue's army, and with Kou Luo and others welcomed Zhou Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: Shao abandoned his post and rode to Yue's camp to join Kou Luo and others in welcoming Zhou Wendi.

sentences.zh: 悅平，以功授大都督、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chenyue was pacified, by merit he was invested as Grand Commander-in-Chief and Regional Inspector of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenyue was subdued, he was rewarded with the posts of Grand Commander and Regional Inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 紹請留所領兵以助東討，請單騎赴州。

translations.literal: Shao requested to leave the troops he commanded to assist the eastern punitive campaign and asked to go to the province alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Shao asked to leave his troops for the eastern campaign and ride alone to take up his province.

sentences.zh: 刺史李叔仁擁州逆命，紹遂歸。

translations.literal: The Regional Inspector Li Shuren held the province in defiance of orders, and Shao thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governor Li Shuren held Liang in rebellion, so Shao turned back.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年，以紹為渭州刺史，進爵昌國伯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, Shao was made Regional Inspector of Wei Province and advanced in rank to Marquis of Changguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was appointed Regional Inspector of Wei and raised to Marquis of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 初，紹為岳長史，周文為岳左丞，及居相，常以恩舊接之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shao had been Yue's Chief Clerk and Zhou Wen had been Yue's Left Assistant; when Zhou Wen held the chancellorship, he often received Shao with favor from old ties.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shao had been Yue's chief clerk while Zhou Wen was his left aide; when Zhou Wen became chancellor, he treated Shao as an old friend.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 紹性好施，祿賜皆分贍親故，及死日，無以送終。

translations.literal: Shao by nature loved to give; salary and grants he divided entirely to support kin and old friends, and at his death there was nothing for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was generous by nature; he gave away salaries and gifts to kin and friends, and at his death there was nothing left for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 兼敬信佛道，遣敕其子曰：「吾本鄉葬法，必殺犬馬，於亡者無益。

translations.literal: Moreover he revered and had faith in the Buddhist Way, leaving instructions to his son, saying, "The burial customs of our homeland require killing dogs and horses, which does the dead no good.
translations.idiomatic: He also revered the Buddhist faith and left his son word: "Our native burial rites call for slaughtering dogs and horses, which helps the dead not at all.

sentences.zh: 汝宜斷之，斂以時服，事從約儉。」

translations.literal: You should cut this off; let the encoffining use present-day garments, and the affairs follow simplicity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: You must put an end to that; dress me in my ordinary clothes and keep the rites plain.

sentences.zh: 還葬長安，天子素服臨吊，贈太尉，賜東園秘器。

translations.literal: He was returned for burial in Chang'an; the Son of Heaven in plain white garments came to mourn; he was posthumously given Grand Commandant and bestowed Eastern Garden secret vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Chang'an; the emperor came in mourning dress, posthumously appointed him Grand Commandant, and granted him the imperial funeral regalia.

sentences.zh: 子渙。

translations.literal: His son Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Huan.

sentences.zh: 毛遐，字鴻遠，北地三原人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xia, style name Hongyuan, was a native of Sanyuan in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xia, styled Hongyuan, was from Sanyuan in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 世為酋帥。

translations.literal: For generations his family were tribal chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: His family had led the tribes for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖天愛，太武時，至定州刺史、始昌子。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tian'ai, in the time of Emperor Taiwu, reached the posts of Regional Inspector of Ding Province and Viscount of Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tian'ai, under Emperor Taiwu, rose to Regional Inspector of Ding and Viscount of Shichang.

sentences.zh: 傳至遐，四世不絕。

translations.literal: The lineage was transmitted to Xia, four generations without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: The line had continued unbroken for four generations down to Xia.

sentences.zh: 正光中，蕭寶夤為大都督，討關中諸賊，咸陽太守韋遂時為都督，以遐為都督府長史。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang, Xiao Baoyin was Grand Commander-in-Chief, campaigning against the various rebels in Guanzhong; Wei Suishi, Governor of Xianyang, was Commander, and Xia was made Chief Clerk of the commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era Xiao Baoyin, as Grand Commander, campaigned against the Guanzhong rebels; Wei Suishi of Xianyang, as overall commander, made Xia chief clerk of his staff.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗還長安，三輔騷擾。

translations.literal: Baoyin was defeated and returned to Chang'an; the Three Adjuncts were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was beaten back to Chang'an, the capital region fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 遐因辭遂還北地，與弟鴻賓聚鄉曲豪傑，遂東西略地，氐、羌多赴之，共推鴻賓為盟主。

translations.literal: Xia thereupon took leave of Suishi and returned to Beidi; with his younger brother Hongbin he gathered the bold men of the countryside, then ranged east and west seizing territory; the Di and Qiang for the most part came to them, and together they made Hongbin alliance leader.
translations.idiomatic: Xia resigned, returned to Beidi, and with his brother Hongbin rallied local champions; they seized territory east and west as Di and Qiang flocked in and made Hongbin their alliance chief.

sentences.zh: 既而賊帥宿勤買奴自號京兆王於北地，遐詐降之，而與鴻賓攻其壁。

translations.literal: Before long the rebel chief Suqin Mainu declared himself King of Jingzhao in Beidi; Xia feigned surrender to him, then with Hongbin attacked his ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Suqin Mainu declared himself King of Jingzhao in Beidi; Xia pretended submission, then with Hongbin stormed his forts.

sentences.zh: 賊自相斫射，縱兵追擊，七柵皆平。

translations.literal: The rebels hacked and shot each other among themselves; he loosed troops in pursuit, and seven stockades were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned on each other; he pursued, and seven stockades fell.

sentences.zh: 後寶夤構逆謀，遐知之，乃寄書與鴻賓，索馬迎接，復于馬祗柵建旗鼓以拒寶夤，攻其將盧祖遷，禽之。

translations.literal: Later when Baoyin formed a treasonous plot, Xia knew it; he then sent a letter to Hongbin asking for horses to receive him, again at Mazhi stockade raised banners and drums to resist Baoyin, attacked his general Lu Zuqian, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin plotted rebellion, Xia warned Hongbin by letter and called for horses; at Mazhi stockade he raised banners against Baoyin, attacked his general Lu Zuqian, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 寶夤以是日拜南郊，竊號。

translations.literal: Baoyin that day performed the suburban altar rite and usurped the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Baoyin performed the suburban rites and proclaimed himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 禮未畢而告敗，寶夤懼，口乾色變，不遑部伍，人皆亂還。

translations.literal: Before the rite was finished defeat was reported; Baoyin was afraid, his mouth dry and complexion changed; he had no leisure to array his ranks, and men all fled back in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rites were finished came news of defeat; Baoyin's mouth went dry and his face went pale; he could not reform his ranks, and his men scattered.

sentences.zh: 詔授遐南幽州刺史，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xia Regional Inspector of Southern You Province and advanced his enfeoffment to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regional Inspector of Southern You and raised to a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 遐又攻破其將侯終德。

translations.literal: Xia again defeated his general Hou Zhongde.
translations.idiomatic: Xia also defeated his general Hou Zhongde.

sentences.zh: 寶夤知內外勢異，輕將十數騎走巴中。

translations.literal: Baoyin knew the situation within and without was different; with a light escort of a dozen or more horsemen he fled to Bazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how the tide had turned, Baoyin fled to Bazhong with only a dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 冬，万俟醜奴陷秦州，詔以遐兼尚書，二州行台。

translations.literal: In winter, Moqi Chounu took Qin Province; an edict made Xia concurrent Minister of the Masters of Writing and Regional Inspector of the two provinces' Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Moqi Chounu took Qin, Xia was made concurrent Minister of the Masters of Writing and head of the two provinces' Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝入關，敕周文帝置二尚書，分掌機事，遐與周惠達始為之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong, he charged Zhou Wendi to establish two Ministers of the Masters of Writing to divide the handling of secret affairs; Xia and Zhou Huida were the first to hold these posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the passes, Zhou Wendi was ordered to set up two Masters of Writing to divide affairs of state—Xia and Zhou Huida were the first appointees.

sentences.zh: 稍遷驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，卒。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to General of Cavalry Who Conquers the West and Pusang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General Who Conquers the West and Pusang, then died.

sentences.zh: 遐少任俠，有智謀。

translations.literal: Xia in his youth was daring and chivalrous and had stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xia was a man of reckless valor and sharp counsel.

sentences.zh: 世為豪右，貲產巨億，士流貧乏者，多被賑贍。

translations.literal: For generations his family were great powerholders, with assets of hundreds of millions; gentlemen of the streams who were poor and wanting were for the most part given relief and support.
translations.idiomatic: A magnate house worth hundreds of millions, they supported many impoverished scholars.

sentences.zh: 故中書郎檀翥、尚書郎公孫范等，常依託之。

translations.literal: Accordingly the Secretariat Gentleman Tan Zhu, the Master of Writing Gentleman Gongsun Fan, and others regularly relied on him for support.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Tan Zhu of the Secretariat and Gongsun Fan of the Masters of Writing often depended on him.

sentences.zh: 至於自供衣食，粗弊而已。

translations.literal: As for clothing and food for himself, they were only coarse and worn.
translations.idiomatic: For himself he wore only the plainest clothes and ate the simplest fare.

sentences.zh: 死之日，鄉黨赴葬，咸共痛惜。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, village and district came to the funeral; all together grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the countryside thronged his funeral and mourned him together.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓大鼻眼，多鬢須，黑而且肥，狀貌頗異，氐、羌見者皆畏之。

translations.literal: Hongbin had a great nose and eyes, many side-whiskers and beard, was black in complexion and moreover stout; his appearance was quite strange, and those of the Di and Qiang who saw him all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongbin had a huge nose, heavy brows and beard, a dark, corpulent frame, and an uncanny look that frightened Di and Qiang alike.

sentences.zh: 加膽略騎射，

translations.literal: Added to this were daring, stratagem, horsemanship, and archery,
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and skilled in horsemanship and archery,

sentences.zh: 俶儻不拘小節，昆季之中，尤輕財好施。

translations.literal: unconventional and not bound by small proprieties; among the brothers he was especially light with property and loved to give.
translations.idiomatic: free-spirited and heedless of convention, and readiest of the brothers to give away his wealth.

sentences.zh: 遐雖云早立，而名出其下。

translations.literal: Though Xia was said to have risen early, his fame was below Hongbin's.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xia had risen first, Hongbin's name outshone his.

sentences.zh: 及賊起，鄉里推為盟主，常與遐一守一戰。

translations.literal: When bandits rose, the countryside pushed Hongbin as alliance leader; he and Xia regularly took turns, one guarding and one fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion spread the countryside made Hongbin alliance chief; the brothers split duties, one holding ground, one fighting.

sentences.zh: 後拜岐州刺史、散騎常侍、開國縣侯。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province, Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Marquis of Kaiguo County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Regional Inspector of Qi, Palace Attendant, and Marquis of Kaiguo.

sentences.zh: 遐笑謂鴻賓曰：「擊賊之功，吾不居汝後，至於受賞，汝在吾前，當以德濟物，不及汝故。」

translations.literal: Xia laughed and said to Hongbin, "In merit for striking the rebels I do not rank behind you; but as for receiving reward, you are before me—because I ought by virtue to aid things, I do not equal you in this.
translations.idiomatic: Xia laughed and told Hongbin, "In fighting rebels I am not behind you—but in rewards you go ahead of me, because I lack your gift for winning men.

sentences.zh: 明帝以鴻賓兄弟所定處多，乃改北地郡為北雍州，鴻賓為刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, because the places the Hongbin brothers had secured were many, therefore changed Beidi Commandery to Northern Yong Province and made Hongbin Regional Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, noting how much land the brothers had secured, made Beidi into Northern Yong Province and Hongbin its governor.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「此以晝錦榮卿也。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "This is to honor you with the glory of returning home by day.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "This is your glory of coming home in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 改三原縣為建中郡，以旌其兄弟。

translations.literal: Sanyuan County was changed to Jianzhong Commandery to commend the brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyuan was made Jianzhong Commandery in their honor.

sentences.zh: 後爾硃天光自關中還洛，夷夏心所忌者，皆將自隨。

translations.literal: Later when Erzhu Tenguang returned from Guanzhong to Luoyang, those whom the hearts of barbarians and Chinese feared were all to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tenguang later left Guanzhong for Luoyang, every man the frontier peoples dreaded was ordered to go with him.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓亦領鄉中壯武二千人以從。

translations.literal: Hongbin also led two thousand stalwart warriors of the countryside to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hongbin brought two thousand of his village braves along.

sentences.zh: 洛中素聞其名，衣冠貧冗者，競與之交。

translations.literal: In Luoyang his name had long been heard; gentlemen in caps and gowns who were poor and straitened vied to join his acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had long known his name; poor scholars crowded to know him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜西袞州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Regional Inspector of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Regional Inspector of Western Yan.

sentences.zh: 羈寓倦遊之輩，四座常滿，鴻賓資給衣食，與己悉同。

translations.literal: Guests dwelling far from home and wearied wanderers filled his four seats without cease; Hongbin supplied food and clothing, treating guests the same as himself in all things.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles and wandering guests packed his hall; Hongbin fed and clothed them as he did himself.

sentences.zh: 私物不足，頗有公費。

translations.literal: His private goods were insufficient; he drew considerably on public funds.
translations.idiomatic: His private purse could not keep pace; he dipped often into public funds.

sentences.zh: 轉南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regional Inspector of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Southern Qing as regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徵還，為有司所糾，鴻賓遂逃匿人間。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled; he was impeached by the responsible offices, and Hongbin then fled and hid among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled; the authorities impeached him, and Hongbin went into hiding among the people.

sentences.zh: 月餘，特詔原之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, a special edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: A month later an extraordinary edict restored him to grace.

sentences.zh: 及孝武帝與齊神武有隙，令鴻賓鎮潼關，為西道之寄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu and Duke Shenwu of Qi came into conflict, he ordered Hongbin to garrison Tong Pass as the reliance of the western route.
translations.idiomatic: When strife opened between Emperor Xiaowu and Gao Huan, Hongbin was put in command of Tong Pass as the linchpin of the western front.

sentences.zh: 車駕西幸，漿糗乏絕，侍官三二日間，唯飲澗水。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went west in fortune, fermented drink and dry rations were utterly exhausted; for two or three days the attending officials drank only stream water.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's flight west, wine and grain ran out; for days his attendants drank nothing but brook water.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓奉獻酒食，迎于稠桑，文武從者，始解饑渴。

translations.literal: Hongbin presented wine and food, received him at Chousang, and the civil and military followers at last relieved hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Hongbin brought food and wine and met the court at Chousang; only then did the civil and military train ease their hunger and thirst.

sentences.zh: 武帝把其手曰：「寒鬆勁草，所望於卿也。

translations.literal: The Emperor took his hand and said, "The hardy pine and tough grass—that is what I expect of you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his hand and said, "You are the winter pine and frost-defying grass I have longed for.

sentences.zh: 事平之日，甯忘主人。」

translations.literal: When affairs are settled, never forget your lord.
translations.idiomatic: When peace returns, do not forget who placed his trust in you.

sentences.zh: 仍留守潼關。

translations.literal: He was left to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then remained to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 後神武來寇，見禽至并州，憂恚卒。

translations.literal: Later when Shenwu came to attack, Hongbin was taken captive and brought to Bing Province, where he died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan later attacked, Hongbin was captured and sent to Bing, where he died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓弟鴻顯，位散騎常侍，封縣侯。

translations.literal: Hongbin's younger brother Hongxian held the post of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was enfeoffed as Marquis of a county.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hongxian served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was made a county marquis.

sentences.zh: 遐乳母所產也，一字七寶。

translations.literal: Xia's wet nurse had given birth to him; his alternate name was Qibao.
translations.idiomatic: He was a son born to Xia's wet nurse and bore the alternate name Qibao.

sentences.zh: 遐養之為弟，因姓毛氏。

translations.literal: Xia raised him as a younger brother, and he therefore took the surname Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Xia raised him as a younger brother, and he took the Mao surname.

sentences.zh: 勁悍多力，後隨諸兄戰鬥，多先鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: Fierce and powerful, he later followed his elder brothers in battle and often led the van in charging the lines.
translations.idiomatic: Tough and immensely strong, he later fought with his brothers and often spearheaded the assault.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，為廣州刺史，與駱超鎮東陽，陷東魏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong he was Regional Inspector of Guang Province; with Luo Chao he garrisoned Dongyang and fell to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong he became Regional Inspector of Guang; garrisoning Dongyang with Luo Chao, he was overrun by Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died there.

sentences.zh: 子野叉。

translations.literal: His son was Yecha.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yecha.

sentences.zh: 乙弗朗，字通照，其先東部人也。

translations.literal: Yi Fulang, styled Tongzhao, was by origin a man of the Eastern Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Fulang, courtesy name Tongzhao, was descended from the Eastern Tribes.

sentences.zh: 世為部落大人，與魏徙代，後因家上樂焉。

translations.literal: For generations his family were chieftains of the tribe; they moved west with Wei to Dai and later made their home at Shangyue.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had long been tribal chiefs; they migrated with Wei to Dai and later settled at Shangyue.

sentences.zh: 朗少有俠氣，在鄉里以善騎射稱。

translations.literal: Lang in youth had a chivalrous spirit and in his village was renowned for skill at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Lang had a bold, chivalrous temper and was known in the countryside for horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 孝莊末，北邊擾亂，避地居並、肆間。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign the northern frontier was in turmoil; he fled and dwelt between Bing and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern frontier collapsed late in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he took refuge between Bing and Xi.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮見而重之，甚相接待，以功封連勺子。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong saw him and valued him, received him with great courtesy, and for merit enfeoffed him as Baron of Lianqu.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong took notice of him, treated him with marked regard, and for his service made him Baron of Lianqu.

sentences.zh: 後隸賀拔嶽，從爾硃天光西討，為岳左廂都督。

translations.literal: Later he entered the service of Heba Yue and followed Erzhu Tianguang on the western campaign, serving as Yue's commander of the left wing.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Heba Yue, joined Erzhu Tianguang on the western campaign, and became Yue's commander of the left wing.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝之禦齊神武，授朗閣內大都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu opposed Duke Shenwu of Qi, Lang was appointed Grand Commander of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu stood against Gao Huan, Lang was made Grand Commander of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 及帝西入，詔朗為軍司，先驅靖路。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the west, an edict made Lang Army Supervisor to go ahead as vanguard and pacify the route.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor moved west, an edict named Lang Army Supervisor to clear the road as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至長安，封長安縣公。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Chang'an he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chang'an county.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Chang'an and was enfeoffed Duke of Chang'an County.

sentences.zh: 卒于岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office as Regional Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Regional Inspector of Qi.

sentences.zh: 初，朗患積冷，周文賜三石東生散，令朗法服之，使人問疾，朝夕相繼，見重如此。

translations.literal: Earlier Lang had suffered chronic cold ailment; Zhou Wen bestowed three piculs of Dongsheng Powder, ordered Lang to take it according to the proper regimen, and sent men to inquire after his illness morning and evening without cease—he was valued to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Lang had long suffered a deep chill; Zhou Wen gave him three piculs of Dongsheng Powder and prescribed its proper use, and messengers inquired after him morning and night without pause—such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 臨終惟云：「恨不見河、洛清平，重反京縣」，以此為恨，三舉手搥床，而便氣盡。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he only said, "I regret not seeing the Yellow River and Luo River at peace and returning again to the capital district," and making this his regret, three times he raised his hands and beat the bed, whereupon his breath was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he said only, "I regret that I shall not see the rivers brought to peace and return once more to the capital," and thrice struck the bed in that grief before his breath failed.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 子鳳，位宮伯、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Feng held the posts of Palace Chief and Grand Master of the Palace with Tally Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng rose to Palace Chief and Grand Master of the Palace, rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 與周閔帝謀宇文護，見殺。

translations.literal: He joined Emperor Min of Zhou in plotting against Yuwen Hu and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted with Emperor Min of Zhou against Yuwen Hu and was executed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：硃瑞以向義受戮，延慶以違順遇禍，各其命焉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Zhu Rui was executed for siding with righteousness; Yanqing met calamity through perversity of compliance; each received his proper fate.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zhu Rui died for standing on the loyal side; Yanqing suffered for twisting obedience to advantage—each met the fate he had chosen.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿屢踐危機，終獲貞吉，豈人謀之所致也？

translations.literal: Hu Sichun repeatedly trod on the brink of peril yet in the end obtained steadfast good fortune—was this really brought about by human contrivance?
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sichun more than once stood at the edge of ruin yet ended in firm fortune—could mere human design have arranged that?

sentences.zh: 徵洽聞強記，以夔、襄任己，終使《咸》、《英》不墜，《韶》、《濩》惟新。

translations.literal: Zheng's broad learning and strong memory took Kui and Xiang as his models, and in the end kept Xian and Ying from falling, while Shao and Hu were made new.
translations.idiomatic: With encyclopedic learning and a prodigious memory, Zheng took the masters Kui and Xiang for his models and kept the ancient hymns Xian and Ying from vanishing while renewing the pieces Shao and Hu.

sentences.zh: 加以盡心所事，無忘直道，抗辭正色，顛沛不渝，蓋有周之忠烈乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, with all his heart in the office he served, he never forgot the straight path; with upright words and stern countenance he did not waver through hardship and wandering—is this not the loyal martyr of Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: He gave his whole heart to his charge, never abandoned the upright path, and spoke frankly with a steady face through every hardship—was he not a true loyalist of the Zhou kind?

sentences.zh: 賈顯智、樊子鵠、侯深等並驅馳風塵之際，但自陷夷戮。

translations.literal: Jia Xianzhi, Fan Zihu, Hou Shen, and others alike galloped through the age of wind and dust, yet themselves fell into extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xianzhi, Fan Zihu, Hou Shen, and the like all raced through turmoil, yet each brought on his own destruction.

sentences.zh: 觀其遺跡，雖獲罪於霸政，求之有魏，得失未可知也。

translations.literal: Considering their traces, though they incurred guilt under a hegemonic regime, weighed in Wei their gains and losses remain hard to judge.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in retrospect, though they offended the ruling power, judged against Wei standards their record is not easy to sum up as pure loss or gain.

sentences.zh: 賀拔允昆季以勇略之資，當馳競之日，並邀時投隙，展效立功。

translations.literal: The brothers of He Bayun, with resources of courage and strategy, in the days of racing contention all seized the moment and found openings, displaying service and establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Heba brothers, gifted with courage and strategy, seized every opening in an age of fierce competition and won merit by action.

sentences.zh: 始則委質爾硃，中乃結款高氏，太昌之後，即帝圖高。

translations.literal: At first they entrusted themselves to the Erzhu clan; midway they formed ties with the Gao house; after Taichang they immediately sought Gaozu's imperial design.
translations.idiomatic: They first pledged to the Erzhu house, then cultivated the Gao clan, and after Taichang threw themselves behind Gaozu's bid for the throne.

sentences.zh: 察其所由，固非守節之士。

translations.literal: Examining the course they took, they were plainly not men who guarded integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed plainly, they were not men of steadfast principle.

sentences.zh: 及勝垂翅江左，憂魏室之危亡；

translations.literal: When Sheng drooped his wings on the Jiang left, he grieved the Wei house's peril and ruin;
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng, wings clipped in the south, grieved for the Wei house in peril;

sentences.zh: 奮翼關西，感梁朝之顧遇，有長者之風矣。

translations.literal: He flapped his wings in Guan west, was moved by the Liang dynasty's gracious treatment, and had the air of an elder of worth.
translations.idiomatic: He spread his wings again in the west, grateful for the Liang court's favor, and showed the bearing of a man of mature virtue.

sentences.zh: 終能保榮持寵，良有以焉。

translations.literal: In the end he could preserve glory and favor—well did he have cause for it.
translations.idiomatic: That he kept his honors to the end is not surprising.

sentences.zh: 嶽以二千羸兵，抗三秦勍敵，奮其智勇，克翦凶渠，雜種畏威，遐方慕義，斯亦一時之盛矣。

translations.literal: Yue with two thousand worn troops resisted the three Qin's fierce enemy, exerted wisdom and courage, was able to cut down the evil ringleader; mixed peoples feared his might and distant regions admired his righteousness—this too was a glory of the age.
translations.idiomatic: With two thousand exhausted troops Heba Yue held off the formidable foes of the three Qin, brought his wisdom and courage to bear, and destroyed a murderous chieftain; mixed tribes feared his might and distant regions admired his justice—a momentary zenith indeed.

sentences.zh: 卒以勳高速禍，無備嬰戮，惜哉！

translations.literal: He finally because merit was high met speedy calamity; without preparation he suffered execution. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his towering merit hastened disaster, and unprepared he met the blade. What a pity!

sentences.zh: 昔陳涉首事不終，有漢因而創業；

translations.literal: Of old Chen She first raised the affair but did not finish; Han thereupon thereby founded the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Chen She launched the uprising but did not live to finish it; the Han arose from that beginning.

sentences.zh: 賀拔功成夙殞，周文籍以開基。

translations.literal: Heba's achievement was accomplished yet early perished; Zhou Wen by it borrowed to open the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue's founding merit perished early; Zhou Wen built on it to open his dynasty.

sentences.zh: 不有所廢，君何以興？

translations.literal: "If nothing is discarded, how can the lord rise?"
translations.idiomatic: "If one man is not set aside, how can the ruler rise?"

sentences.zh: 信乎其然矣。

translations.literal: Surely it is so indeed.
translations.idiomatic: How true that proved.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅肆行殘慝，死不旋踵，觀其亡滅，蓋自取之。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue wantonly practiced cruel wickedness and before the heel could turn death arrived; considering his ruin and extinction, he surely brought it on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue practiced cruelty without restraint and died almost at once; his fall was plainly of his own making.

sentences.zh: 念賢有始有卒，取敬群公。

translations.literal: Nian Xian had beginning and end, winning respect among the assembled nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Nian Xian began well and ended well, and won the regard of the great lords.

sentences.zh: 梁覽終以取禍，鮮克之義。

translations.literal: Liang Lan in the end met calamity—the meaning of "few can finish well."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Lan ended in disaster—fitting the old truth that few finish well.

sentences.zh: 雷紹馳騖雲雷之秋，毛遐兄弟致力經綸之日，乙弗朗輾轉擾攘之中，卒獲歸順，美矣！

translations.literal: Lei Shao galloped through the autumn of clouds and thunder; the brothers Mao Xia devoted themselves in the days of state planning; Yi Fulang turned through turmoil and disturbance—and in the end all obtained submission and return. Beautiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Lei Shao raced through thunderous times; the Mao brothers gave their strength in the days of founding the state; Yi Fulang was tossed through chaos—yet each in the end found his way to allegiance. Admirable, all three!
